Following the death of his maternal grandmother, young Jamie is forced apart from his brother. While his brother is sent to an orphanage, Jamie is moved into his paternal grandmother’s home. Life feels like a silent black-and-white film, and he finds refuge in the cinema, seeking salvation in the Technicolor dreams on the screen. Long before her legendary tenure as Éric Rohmer’s long-time editor, Mary Stephen was already a "tailor of images," using her camera to capture the displacement of the diaspora, the struggle for identity, and the growing pains of coming of age. This screening features four of her early works, including her debut feature *Shades of Silk* and three rare shorts of distinct styles—*Labyrinth*, *A Very Easy Death*, and *Pawaganak: The Great Canadian Puberty Rite*. Through the interplay of sound and image, Stephen transforms personal experience into evocative visual poetry. From a Canadian road-trip baptism and the somniloquy of a Parisian student dorm to a quiet gaze at death, her imagery is as delicate and resilient as silk. These works serve as memory fragments drifting between Eastern and Western cultures, documenting her perception and search for selfhood.

title:為一切人，成為一切:
In 1952, during the arduous post-war years in Taiwan, over a hundred French and Swiss priests chose to serve in the Hualien and Taitung regions—the areas most lacking in resources at the time. They immersed themselves in indigenous communities, living alongside the residents while learning their languages and traditional cultures. In times of hardship, they provided a sanctuary for the local people, dedicating their lives to serving those in need. 

Long before the preservation of indigenous languages became a prominent social issue, these priests had already begun compiling dictionaries and conducting Mass in native tongues, effectively documenting tribal histories. Their work has since become an invaluable historical resource for Taiwan’s cultural and linguistic research. Seventy years later, amidst the shifting tides of Taiwanese society, some priests have been forced to depart, yet Fathers Liu Yi-feng and Dai Hong-ji remain on the front lines, continuing their mission to care for the most vulnerable.

In 1970s Glasgow, a massive garbage strike has left the streets infested with rats and a lingering stench. Twelve-year-old James is playing by the canal with a friend when a sudden accident occurs, causing him to flee in panic and bury his guilt in silence. He spends his days wandering, forming innocent bonds with a bullied, love-starved girl and a naive neighbor boy. Drifting between a dysfunctional home and decaying street corners, he yearns to escape his bleak reality. At night, he dreams of his pet rat ascending into the cosmos on a red balloon; by day, he boards a bus to nowhere, escaping his desolate housing estate to find a moment of peace in the distant fields.

title:狂飆與反叛：畫室外的陳來興、姚瑞中、劉秋兒 ｜陳文彬、姚瑞中、劉秋兒:
Artists who grew up during the Martial Law era found themselves at the heart of a turbulent society when the ban on newspapers was lifted in 1987, Article 100 of the Criminal Code was amended, and street movements began to surge. They threw themselves into these movements, their actions becoming a vibrant presence in the midst of social unrest. During this period, art served as an invisible pillar of support for street activism and social change. Artist Chen Lai-hsing donated works on several occasions at fundraising dinners for Chen Wan-chen—who had secretly returned to Taiwan while on the "blacklist"—and later co-founded the Taiwan Teachers’ Union with Lin Shuang-bu. During the commemorative exhibition for the May 20 Movement, Chen, along with Lin Cho-shui, Wu Mali, and Hou I-cheng, transformed the old Beitou Station into a gallery, treating "the street" as the ultimate venue for their art.

In the 1990s, performance art expanded its impact through the infiltration of public spaces and the promotion of "alternative art spaces," using art as a foundation to collide with social structures. Yao Jui-chung, wandering through landscapes of decay, used his camera to capture various forms of ruins across Taiwan, witnessing the transformation of industrial ruins into cultural and creative parks. For Yao, the restless 1990s became the catalyst for his "Ruin Enlightenment," leading him to write that "everything will become the ruins of the future." Meanwhile, Liu Chiu-er hosted an underground radio station in the 1990s and later established the "Dogpig Art Cafe" in Southern Taiwan, embedding his community energy and artistic activism into the shifting artistic landscape of Kaohsiung.

This forum invites director Chen Wen-pin, who is currently filming a documentary on Chen Lai-hsing, alongside artists Yao Jui-chung and Liu Chiu-er. Together, they will reflect on their firsthand experiences in street art movements and youthful rebellion, while delving into Taiwan's evolution from "spatial de-martialization" to contemporary cultural policy. Through the perspectives of these three speakers, we will re-examine that pivotal era of history and reflect on the core meaning of "art as social infrastructure."

title:畫外流離：革命直至勝利:
Driven by curiosity and a lack of familiarity with Palestinian cinema and history, a film student uses the 1948 "Nakba" (Day of Catastrophe) as a watershed moment, navigating the battles and struggles of the Palestinian people through archival footage. Beginning with classics such as Jean-Luc Godard’s *Notre Musique*, the film pieces together a destiny spanning over 40 years. Composed entirely of Palestinian footage screened at international film festivals prior to 1982, the work directly highlights the techniques and significance of repurposing "displaced images."

A meditation on Palestinian self-representation through the Palestine Film Unit (PFU) of the 1960s–70s. Drawing on globally recovered archival footage, the film traces militant filmmakers reclaiming image and narrative through revolutionary cinema, reflecting on struggles revived on screen—and those that remain off frame.

title:神木之島:
Following *Black Bear Forest*, Golden Horse Award-winning director Li Hsiang-hsiu returns with another documentary capturing the stories of Taiwan's wilderness. The film follows canopy epiphyte researcher Rebecca Hsu and "The Tree Hunters," a team she leads that is dedicated to locating Taiwan’s tallest trees.

Tracking the team’s expeditions, the film traverses Taiwan’s remote wilderness from north to south, including the Chilan Mountains, the upper reaches of the Da’an River, the Taigang River in Bianjiyan, the Taoshan and Shilun Mountain areas, the Daxueshan Forest Road, the Kashe River basin along the Danda Forest Road, the Ka’alang River, and the region around Dagui Lake and Mount Benye.

Beyond documenting the search itself, the film captures the creation of a life-sized portrait of the "Taoshan Giant Tree" and the intricate process of dismantling logging cables. This documentary provides a rare look at how the team locates these giants in the deep wilderness, how they predict tree heights before setting out, and the death-defying climbs required to measure them manually.

title:綠星人大鬧巴黎城:

title:綠洲 4K經典數位修復:

title:綠的海平線+軍教男兒－台灣軍士教導團的故事:
At the end of World War II, more than 8,000 Taiwanese youths were mobilized by the Japanese government to produce military aircraft at naval factories. In the post-war era, they stood in the fissures between different times and regimes; though their chosen paths varied, they all faced the same grueling struggle to adapt and survive. Facing the weight of history, the film avoids resentment and pathos, opting instead for a warm narration to thread together archival documents and interviews. It gently unfolds the personal strivings and helpless drifts of individuals in a turbulent age, reflecting the complex, overlapping layers of identity and belonging.

**Suspended Duty: Taiwan Military Training Regiment**
KUO Liang-yin｜Taiwan｜2010｜DCP｜Colour｜47 min

During the era of "Resisting Communism and Opposing Russia," over 4,000 young men joined the "Taiwan Military Training Regiment" in 1950, expecting to serve as cadres for a new Taiwanese army upon completing their training. Before long, they were hit with a sudden order of "suspended duty," leaving them on standby for over 50 years without ever being formally discharged. Using a satirical, propaganda-style narration to humorously bridge various interviews, the film reveals how political forces discipline the body, silence dissent, and manipulate thought. Through the firsthand accounts of those who lived through different wars, it invites a deeper contemplation on the question: "For whom do we fight?"

title:總統的蛋糕:
★ Iraq’s official entry for the 2026 Academy Award for Best International Feature Film, a dark horse that advanced to the top 15 shortlist.

In 1990 Iraq, war and sanctions have drained the color from the cities, and supplies are so scarce that even sugar has become a luxury. Amidst this hardship, President Saddam Hussein orders the entire nation to celebrate his birthday, decreeing that every school class must present him with a cake or face unimaginable consequences. Nine-year-old Lamia never expected that she would be the one chosen for this daunting task.

Living alone with her grandmother, they can barely afford to bake bread, let alone a grand cake. To save her classmates from punishment, Lamia clutches her beloved rooster and sets off with her grandmother on a journey to the city. What she thought would be a simple trip to gather ingredients turns into a complex and perilous adventure. In the heart of a turbulent city, she witnesses the many faces of adults struggling to survive: the kind and the cunning, those who offer a helping hand, and those who would betray her in a heartbeat.

title:舞林殺手:
Award-winning director Eiji Uchida strikes again with a genre-defying masterpiece that blends high-octane assassin action with the art of dance. A motley crew of professional assassins, each with vastly different ages and temperaments, accepts a high-stakes, big-money contract. Their target is the notorious mob boss Heizo Honjo, but there’s a catch: the only way to get close to him is by winning a dance competition!

With zero experience, no chemistry, and even less motivation, can this ragtag team actually compete in a serious dance tournament? Assembled solely because they supposedly had "prior dance experience," this eccentric squad features: Daiya, an orphanage counselor who is secretly a legendary ex-assassin; Kumashiro, the mission recruiter and second-in-command of the Kazama Syndicate; Kiryu, a cold-blooded lone wolf who hates working in groups; Arata, a hot-headed but fiercely loyal hitman; and Murasame, a washed-up former yakuza. 

Though they initially clash at every turn, these killers soon find themselves seduced by the rhythm, transforming into a formidable force of "dance-floor assassins." As they fight their way through the rounds, will they actually dance their way to the championship?

As they search and compare their finds, they find themselves wanting more and more to take this "beauty" home. A young woman meets a British gentleman in a foreign land, falls head over heels, and marries him in a whirlwind romance. However, upon returning to his grand estate in Cornwall, she discovers the ancient manor is no honeymoon nest, but a labyrinth haunted by the shadow of his late wife. From the furnishings and old clothes to every corner of the house, everything seems to whisper her presence. As the young bride sinks into anxiety, the ice-cold housekeeper constantly reminds her that she can never replace her predecessor. When a shipwreck is salvaged and brought ashore, the lies and mysteries of death hidden deep within the estate begin to surface.

Alfred Hitchcock’s first American film, adapted from Daphne du Maurier’s 1938 novel of the same name, uses high-contrast black-and-white cinematography to recreate a world of suspense and obsession. Despite the strict constraints of the Hays Code, the film subtly touches on taboos such as marital infidelity and lesbian undertones. Du Maurier, a master of Gothic romance, possessed a style so influential that it inspired the novel *Mistress of Milan* (the basis for *Corpse Bride*) and even led some to believe she was its true author.
title:蠱降: Malaysian real estate mogul Song Longchen uses Thai black magic to seize land development rights, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. Fon deduces they have fallen victim to a curse and seeks the aid of the venerable Master Bai. title:街頭巷尾（數位修復版）:
1963 Golden Horse Award for Best Child Star. After the impoverished Lin A-sao passes away from illness, she leaves behind her young daughter, Xiao Zhu, with no one to turn to. Shi Santai, a scavenger, takes the girl under his wing. Together with pedicab driver Chen A-fa and the other residents of their crowded tenement courtyard, they support one another amidst the dilapidated alleys. As poverty, illness, and emotional entanglements strike in succession, can these ordinary people protect their way of life and each other?

This film was Lee Hsing’s first Mandarin-language feature and a pivotal turning point in his early career. He spent considerable time scouting locations and observing people, even leading the crew to scavenge old furniture for the sets in an effort to create a believable world within the tenement. Although primarily in Mandarin, the film retains fragments of Taiwanese Hokkien and features Hokkien cinema star Ho Yu-hua, leaving clear traces of Lee’s roots in Hokkien filmmaking. Cinematographer Lai Cheng-ying crafted meticulous visuals, marking the beginning of a long-term partnership between the two. By focusing on the slums and the working class, the film offers an early glimpse into the themes of social conditions, family ethics, and community bonds that would define Lee Hsing’s later work.

Instead of calling the police, she calmly cleans the scene, replaces his name with hers on the manuscript, and sends it to a publisher. Thus begins her journey. She and her best friend flee the cold, gloomy skies of Scotland for the sun-drenched coast of Spain. Wandering through disjointed and unfamiliar landscapes, she begins to grasp the root of her emptiness and the restless urge for self-exile. 

Adapted from the Somerset Maugham Award-winning novel, the film serves as a contemporary variation of Camus’s *The Stranger*. With a minimalist narrative and captivating cinematography, it dives deep into the protagonist’s strange state, oscillating between mourning and revelry. The film’s soundscape is driven by the boyfriend’s mixtape, featuring tracks by The Velvet Underground and Aphex Twin, using fragmented light and rhythm to articulate alienation and the drifting soul of a woman with nowhere to belong.
title:讓建築歌唱～徐亞英的交響人生:
Renowned Chinese-American architectural acoustics master Xu Yaying spent decades collaborating with Pritzker Prize-winning legends such as I.M. Pei and Frank Gehry. Celebrated for his "invisible" acoustic designs, Xu contributed to the design and construction of nearly a hundred cultural and artistic venues worldwide. His late-career magnum opus—and the project he takes the most pride in—is Taiwan’s National Kaohsiung Center for the Arts (Weiwuying).

Architectural acoustics is a synthesis of physics, music, architecture, and science. An acoustician enables music to flow through a meticulously designed space, ensuring that beautiful melodies can truly move the human heart. Following Xu’s lean yet steady footsteps, we revisit his most iconic masterpieces, including the Louvre Pyramid and the Philharmonie Luxembourg. He recounts his journey of solving complex challenges for architects, revealing how he earned the nickname "Mr. Why Not" from Christian de Portzamparc.

title:豬八戒與孫悟空:
Tang Sanzang and his disciples journey westward to retrieve sacred scriptures. Along the way, demons lay one trap after another, and Pigsy finds himself repeatedly swayed by worldly temptations. From the Mo Family Manor to the Silk Cave, the bond between the master and his disciples is frequently strained. How will the ever-troublesome Pigsy join forces with Sun Wukong to turn danger into safety?

Continuing the slapstick comedic style of the wildly popular *Brother Wang and Brother Lin on a Tour of Taiwan*, this film stands as one of director Li Hsing’s most significant works from his Taiwanese-language cinema period. The fact that Pigsy’s name precedes Sun Wukong’s in the title reveals the director's fondness for comic figures like Pigsy, as well as his early creative focus on "licorice" (supporting) characters and folk tales. Playing the role of Pigsy is none other than "Brother Wang" himself, Li Kuan-chang, who brings his signature comedic flair to the supernatural world of *Journey to the West*. The film’s songs are performed off-screen by the "Queen of Formosan Songs," Chi Lu-hsia, and others. Accompanied by on-screen lyrics, these musical numbers highlight the symbiotic relationship between Taiwanese-language films and the pop music market, as well as the central role music played in the moviegoing experience of the era. The production was completed at Ho Chi-ming’s Huaxing Studio.
title:超人再起:
A "Superman" is someone who transcends themselves. While the first documentary, *Taiwan Superman*, chronicled those who overcame congenital limitations, *Superman Rising* turns its lens toward heroes facing severe acquired trauma. 

The film features a blind national athlete who shattered long jump records; a firefighter who suffered severe burns in the Kaohsiung gas explosions yet returned to his post; and a one-legged "Ironman" who, after losing a limb in a car accident, now challenges himself in land, sea, and air sports. It is difficult to imagine the immense courage required to navigate such hardships, yet these individuals did more than just endure—following their "rebirth," they reached out to support others walking similar paths. 

Through their stories, we see how scars are transformed into strength and witness the unwavering devotion of their families. We follow the life trajectories of these "Supermen" as they break through the darkness to face the light once more. This film is shared with the hope of continuing the empowering spirit that the *Taiwan Superman* series brings to us all.

title:跨 ‧ 觀音合作社:
**Trans-Guanyin Collective Presents:**

**Dates:** May 23, 2026 – July 5, 2026
**Venue:** Rooms 40 and 53 (2F), Treasure Hill International Artist Village

*Trans-Guanyin* is a curatorial project initiated by the Trans-Guanyin Collective (TGY Collective), originating from the International MA Program in Studies of Arts and Creative Industries at Taipei National University of the Arts (TNUA). Inspired by Guanyin Mountain and the Guanyin Temple located near the university, this site-specific project is primarily hosted at Treasure Hill International Artist Village, with satellite activities extending across various locations in Taipei. Using "Compassion" as its central curatorial motif, the exhibition explores this theme through political and philosophical frameworks.

Taking the Guanyin Temple as an entry point—a site quietly perched on a hillside with a history dating back over three centuries to early Han Chinese settlements—the exhibition draws on the community’s operational logic. It views the area as a form of "democratic commons" where boundaries remain open, coexistence unfolds, and diverse encounters expand into a multi-sensory field of perception.

"Trans-Guanyin" signifies a cultural movement that crosses boundaries; it is not a fixed state, but a continuous process of transforming relationships. This state resonates with the "becoming" of Avalokiteśvara, whose iconographic transformation is not a mere substitution of male for female, but a condition of existence that transcends binary structures. Thus, *Trans-Guanyin* is understood not as a fixed identity, but as a process of "co-becoming."

By viewing Guanyin as art and as "skillful means" (*upaya*), the project asks: How can the world be redirected through mediated action? This mirrors the curatorial gesture of remaining sensitive and responsive. The spirit of *Trans-Guanyin* emerges through the participation of artists, curators, audiences, and local residents, extending across their roles and relationships. It allows "care" and "cure" to become shared states and a fluid context, pointing toward our existence as beings in transformation—mirrors reflecting one another, collectively constituting the ontological state of "co-becoming."

title:重演缺牙鋼琴實驗工作坊｜國立臺北藝術大學美術學院師生:
At the end of 1999, Liu Chiu-er left the Taipei art scene and returned to Kaohsiung to establish the Dogpig Art Cafe. Unlike the professionalized "alternative spaces" that catered to established artists, Dogpig Art Cafe emphasized a philosophy where anyone could freely present visual art, music, and performances simply by signing up. This diverse array of activities operated continuously without censorship. The "Gap-Toothed Piano" was a dilapidated piano kept at the cafe; despite its broken strings and exposed internal structure, participants never lost interest in playing it. Through recurring programs developed around the instrument—such as the "Sheep-Hitting Show," "Ecstasy Day," and "Labor Art"—the Gap-Toothed Piano evolved from an artist’s personal plaything into a "relational object" that helped build the Dogpig Art Cafe community.

**Instructors:** Kuo Chao-lan, Sun Song-rong
**Time:** 06/14 (Sun) 14:00
**Location:** United Restaurant Exhibition Space, 1F

The "Re-enacting the Gap-Toothed Piano Experimental Workshop" is hosted by Kuo Chao-lan, guest curator of *WE Are Becoming*, and Professor Sun Song-rong of the Graduate Institute of Trans-disciplinary Arts at TNUA. This project brings the classroom directly into the exhibition space. The teaching plan began with students collectively studying "Dogpig Maru," a set of archives from the Dogpig Art Cafe. On the day of the workshop, students will present their re-enactment plans for the Gap-Toothed Piano on-site. The "critique" sessions common in art schools will be relocated to the exhibition hall, where participants will have the opportunity to witness or co-perform the actions based on student proposals. Key figures from the original cultural scene will also be invited to participate in the critique.

Online registration required; free admission.
▶︎ Registration Link

**Speaker Bios**

**▍Kuo Chao-lan**
Curator of the 2026 C-LAB Annual Exhibition and Associate Professor in the Department of Fine Arts at Taipei National University of the Arts (TNUA). Her teaching and research focus on contemporary art, art history, and curatorial practice. Her interests revolve around the dynamics of art circulation, historiography, and contemporary art within exhibition culture. Her recent curatorial projects strive to practice "perceptible art historiography"—an art history oriented toward the public.

**▍Sun Song-rong**
Professor and Director of the Graduate Institute of Trans-disciplinary Arts at TNUA. He has recently served as the curator for exhibitions such as *Walker: Tsai Ming-liang*, *The Dawn of Video Art in Taiwan: 1980s-1990s*, and *Edward Yang: A Retrospective*. His primary research fields include contemporary Sinophone film aesthetics, the intersection of film and contemporary art, and contemporary French film theory. He is the author of *In-Sight/Out-of-Sight: The Image Art and Cross-disciplinary Practices of Tsai Ming-liang* and *The Cinematic Power of Taiwan: Six Cross-disciplinary Image Arts in Search of Cinema*.

title:野沈浸:
**Wild Immersion**

**Dates:** 2026-05-21 ~ 2026-07-12
**Venue:** Treasure Hill International Artist Village, Frontier 52/54, Gallery B1

In his 1967 essay *Art and Objecthood*, Michael Fried identified "theatricality" as an inherent threat to modernist art. To him, the strategy of incorporating the viewer's physical body into a spatio-temporal situation—creating a sense of envelopment and extension—was an erosion of the self-sufficient purity of visual aesthetics. 

Yet, the paradox of history is that this very "theatricality" became the most powerful liberating force for installation art in the following decades, establishing "presence" itself as the core site of meaning production. 

The common predicament of contemporary immersive exhibitions lies precisely in the over-domestication of this theatricality: light is precisely calibrated, movement is softly guided, and sensory stimuli are carefully controlled within a pleasant threshold. Within these spaces, the viewer relaxes and drops their guard, but consequently loses the capacity to be truly shaken. This form of immersion is comfortable—an "experience commodity" in the consumerist sense. It utilizes illusionism to create a beautiful bubble parallel to reality, inviting the viewer to temporarily forget themselves.

However, forgetting oneself is never synonymous with true presence. 

*Wild Immersion* pursues an alternative ideal depicted in Antonin Artaud’s "Theatre of Cruelty": not to paralyze the viewer with gentle illusions, but to awaken the body through the impact of real perception, making presence an unavoidable tremor. Artaud’s "cruelty" never refers to literal violence; rather, it points toward a fundamental honesty of perception—a refusal to let art become a substitute for reality, and an insistence that every encounter be a genuine collision.

Every work in this exhibition features a built-in degree of "loss of control": sensor misreadings, algorithmic drifts, and the physical noise of the materials themselves. These "flaws" are not technical omissions but strategic ethical manifestos—a stance the exhibition takes against becoming an "illusion machine." 

It is precisely in the cracks of system failure, at the moment expectations fall short, that the automated programs of habitual perception are forcibly interrupted. The viewer exits the role of the consumer and re-confronts the uncategorizable with a vulnerable body. "Wild" serves here as the core aesthetic methodology—wild things do not grow according to design intent; they sprawl, escape, and develop unforeseen logic within the gaps. The exhibition pits the wild against the tamed, loss of control against optimization, and friction against the seamless. Ultimately, in a coarser and more physically weighted manner, it fulfills the true promise of immersion: not to lead you into a more beautiful illusion, but to allow you to live in the present in a more naked way.

***

title:銀河補習班:
★ 2019 Macau International Movie Festival: 3 nominations including Best Film and Best Actor ★ 2019 China Film Critics Association Awards: Top Ten Films of the Year; Nominated for Best Film and Best Director ★ Directed by and starring Deng Chao, Golden Rooster Best Actor for *The Dead End*.

In the vastness of space, astronaut Ma Fei unexpectedly loses contact with Earth. In his moment of despair, he finds himself reminiscing about his father, Ma Haowen. Once the brilliant engineer behind the Dongpei Bridge, Ma Haowen’s life spiraled downward after he was imprisoned for taking the fall for a professional disaster when Ma Fei was a child. Upon his release, he discovers his son is at the bottom of his class and facing expulsion by Director Yan for chronic truancy. Ma Haowen strikes a bet with the director: if Ma Fei can break into the top ten, he stays in school. While Director Yan prioritizes academic success above all else, Ma Haowen encourages his son to chase his dreams. Can Ma Haowen’s unconventional and passionate approach change his son’s destiny? And will astronaut Ma Fei find his way back to Earth to reunite with his father? Spanning decades, this heartwarming and emotional journey of a father and son rediscovers the warmth and miracles of life.
title:鍵:
1959 Kinema Junpo Top 10 Japanese Films (9th Place)
1960 Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film
1960 Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize

Antique appraiser Kenmochi, in a desperate bid to defy aging, devises a dangerous scheme: he maneuvers Kimura, his daughter’s physician fiancé, into an affair with his wife, Ikuko, hoping that jealousy will reignite his waning virility. As the voyeuristic perspectives shift, the prim wife’s awakening desires, the future son-in-law’s restless ambition, and the daughter’s cold detachment all come to light. In this web of calculated lust, what fate awaits them?

Marking his second consecutive collaboration with director Kon Ichikawa, Tatsuya Nakadai delivers a chillingly intellectual performance as Kimura. This sinister turn stands in stark contrast to his moralistic role in *The Human Condition*, cementing his reputation for versatility between hero and villain. Adapted from Jun'ichiro Tanizaki’s novel, Ichikawa and screenwriters Natto Wada and Keiji Hasebe transform the original’s dark, aesthetic eroticism into a biting black comedy. Captured through Kazuo Miyagawa’s highly stylized cinematography, the film uses light and shadow to maintain a clinical, detached gaze on the characters' spiraling desires.
title:鏡之第三樂章: ★ A Cahiers du Cinéma Top 10 Film of 2025. While on a weekend getaway, piano student Laura is involved in a car accident. Though she emerges physically unscathed, her boyfriend is killed, leaving her consumed by shock and a profound sense of emptiness. In the German countryside, she encounters a woman who witnessed the crash. Struck by Laura’s resemblance to her own late daughter, the woman kindly takes her into her idyllic family home. However, this seemingly warm sanctuary is fraught with unspoken projections and substitutions. As the woman attempts to fill the void of her loss with Laura, the young student begins to feel suffocated by the weight of the care and expectations thrust upon her.
title:門對門移動書店:
Based on the heartwarming bestseller that topped the charts for 100 weeks, *The Door-to-Door Bookstore* is a box office sensation that earned over NT$200 million in Germany.

Carl, a dedicated "book walker," lives a life as precise as clockwork. Every day, he follows the exact same path, hand-delivering carefully wrapped books to the doorsteps of his loyal customers. He knows the tastes of everyone in town and takes great pride in his ability to select the perfect book for each person.

One day, Carl’s orderly world is unexpectedly interrupted. Nine-year-old Schascha, who is still healing from the loss of her mother, decides to join Carl on his rounds. Not only does she find solace in the books and the journey, but her unique perspective on life also helps Carl open his heart, sparking an unexpected friendship.

However, a sudden turn of events causes Carl to lose his job. The once-vibrant town, once filled with the fragrance of books, begins to fall into a lonely silence. As the community drifts apart, Schascha decides to rely on the power she believes in most: the magic of a good book to bring people together. Joining forces with Carl, she sets out to create a profound and positive change—not just for their readers, but for themselves as well.
title:開放式（沒）關係:
Best Film, 1978 Valladolid International Film Festival
Nominated for Best Feature, Chicago International Film Festival

Two men and one woman live under the same roof in a bond that transcends boundaries—they are friends, family, and lovers all at once, navigating a warm, unconventional relationship built on trust. Fernand is the househusband who handles the cooking and cleaning, Alexa is the breadwinner, and Louis devotes himself entirely to his music. In their world, true happiness is found less in fleeting desire and more in the way they anchor one another through life’s lows. Their delicate balance is shifted when Fernand unexpectedly brings home a beautiful young woman, turning their trio into a lively household of four.

Coline Serreau’s debut feature film tenderly embraces taboo subjects, yet this suburban Parisian utopia almost never made it to the big screen. In the 1970s, Serreau faced constant rejection for her "scandalous" script. Through sheer persistence, she eventually secured the funding to bring this story to life, offering audiences a glimpse into a polyamorous relationship that is purer and more profound than any typical love triangle.
title:阿嘉莎的四季:
★ Best Canadian Feature Documentary, International Documentary Film Festival
★ Official Selection, International Documentary Film Festival

On the vast plains of Manitoba, Canada, elderly Agatha Bock lives alone on her 54-acre family farm. There is no running water, no cell phone, and even the landline barely functions. Without a driver’s license or a car, Agatha has constructed a self-sufficient "handmade universe." She tills the earth by hand and preserves heirloom seeds passed down through generations. Watermelons, beans, flowers, herbs, and vegetables flourish under her care, reflecting her commitment to order and her profound agricultural wisdom. Living with a pure and independent spirit, Agatha breathes in rhythm with the land, composing a poem of life that spans the four seasons.

Directed by Agatha’s niece, contemporary artist Emily Atkins, and filmed by an all-female crew over six years, the film captures Agatha’s life from age 86 to 90. Shot entirely on 16mm film, the documentary retains a grainy, tactile quality that mirrors Agatha’s hands-on daily labor. This is more than just a record of aging; it is a visual almanac blending the mundane with the artistic—a poem of life unfolding across the seasons.
title:阿弗雷找新家: Displaced by war, Alfred is forced to flee his home with all his belongings. He goes from door to door seeking help, only to be rejected time and time again. That is, until he meets a kind soul who offers him a warm cup of coffee and the comfort of companionship.
title:限量優惠！真愛挑日子One: Life is defined by countless "July 15ths." If there were only one day a year that allowed you to witness love in all its many forms, how would you spend it? Emma and Dexter met on their graduation day and promised to see each other on this date every year. Sometimes, they are best friends who share everything; other times, they are each other’s strongest support. But they always seem to say the right things at the wrong time—and when the time is finally right, they miss each other once again.
title:陽光女子合唱團: Once women of the underworld, they now use their most brilliant voices to sing an unforgettable confession to the ones they love. Imprisoned by a cruel twist of fate, these women find strength in one another, supporting each other as they rediscover hope for the future.
title:隱蹟之書：重寫自我:
Toronto IFF 2025
IDFA 2025
Golden Horse Awards: Best Documentary Feature & Best Editing

Veteran editor Mary Stephen possesses a distinctly East Asian face yet bears a Western surname: Stephen. Delving into her family’s little-known history through her father’s journals, she discovers that both her parents lived under assumed names with pasts where truth and fiction blur. Her father appears to be a descendant of Australian Aboriginal fishermen, while her mother—a woman who once harbored literary dreams—seems to have had a subtle connection to a romance in China involving a member of Virginia Woolf’s family.

In her quest to uncover the origins of the "Stephen" name, she sifts through home movies and old photographs, reconstructing a private family history that feels truer than reality itself amidst an era of colonial expansion and upheaval. Navigating a maze of multiple narratives, she interrogates her own identity, exploring how individuals can find flight once more through the fog of diaspora by rewriting their own history. Together, she pieces together a profound cinematic portrait of life spanning borders and a century of global change.
title:雙囍:
"Today is our wedding day; shouldn't it be the happiest day of our lives?" 

Between divorced parents and a superstitious father-in-law, the result is two weddings in a single day—and the guests from both sides are strictly forbidden from seeing one another! When the bride and groom, who should be the stars of the show, find themselves playing supporting roles just to fulfill their elders' wishes, how can these two "weddings of the century" possibly succeed? Amidst high-stakes missions and non-stop blunders, one promise remains: no matter how much chaos ensues today, we will face every moment together.
title:雞舍裡的卡皮巴拉: A family of capybaras flees to a chicken coop for shelter, but the chickens find them "so strange!" Unexpectedly, a little chick reaches out a wing and says, "Hi! I want to be your friend." From that day on, a new kind of laughter filled the farm. For when we learn to open our hearts, the world becomes a little bit wider.
title:離別沒有吉時 索: Ming-ching is a single father who dreams of stardom. One day, he wakes up in his childhood home only to discover his family is holding his funeral. Faced with his own death, he realizes he never said a proper goodbye to his daughter, yet his every attempt to reach her fails. Caught between the worlds of the living and the dead, the two are unable to speak, but they slowly begin to understand one another. Through this long-overdue connection, they come to realize that there is no "perfect time" for parting—only the importance of loving while there is still time.
title:離岸的船 索: During the Japanese occupation of the Korean Peninsula, over 3,000 Koreans came to work in Taiwan, which was also a Japanese colony at the time. Following Japan's defeat in 1945, limited repatriation resources left 358 Koreans stranded in Taiwan; most settled in Shengli Lane, Keelung. The film follows three Korean women, now in their seventies, who have been forgotten in the cracks between Korea and Taiwan, their identities caught in a constant struggle between the two nations.
title:離異之域 索: This film chronicles the story of the "Lost Army" of the Yunnan-Burma border and their descendants. More than seventy years ago, these soldiers fought across Yunnan, Burma, and Northern Thailand before eventually retreating to Taiwan in stages. Over time, they came to embrace this foreign land as their new home, weaving together the displaced memories and life journeys of three generations.
title:電影版教場：驪歌: ★ Based on the mystery novel by Hiroki Nagaoka, this film uncovers the hidden, dark truths of the police academy! A #1 box office hit in Japan during its opening week, it has sparked a sensation with rave reviews and unanimous acclaim from audiences!
title:青木瓜之味 索: After years of drifting, 22-year-old Han Reng-ding stepped into Li-Ching Muay Thai and found a sense of belonging he had never known before. Samon, the gym’s Thai head coach, looked after him in both work and life, while the other Thai migrant workers selflessly sparred with him in the ring and shared their lives outside of it. For six years, they lived together like family. However, these tight-knit bonds are about to change as Han begins to plan for his future. Because of this group of Thai friends, Han’s life has taken a path he never could have imagined.
title:飛吧!熊鷹:
A powerful new masterpiece from Liang Chieh-te, the acclaimed director of *Fly, Kite Fly* and master of Taiwanese bird documentaries. Filmed over 12 years across numerous locations, this film is a definitive record of Taiwan’s largest raptor: the Mountain Hawk-Eagle.

Deep within the mountain ranges of Taiwan, the Mountain Hawk-Eagle exists as a figure caught between legend and a fleeting gaze. As the island’s most robust and ethereal bird of prey, it is massive yet elusive—appearing with the majesty of a king and vanishing without a trace. To the Paiwan and Rukai peoples, it is more than just a creature of the sky; it is the incarnation of ancestral spirits. Its feathers symbolize honor and social status, carrying a cultural weight passed down through generations.

Since 2003, scholar Sun Yuan-hsun has ventured into the most remote reaches of the wilderness to begin a long pursuit. Alongside his students and assistants, he has delved into treacherous terrain, navigating slippery mountain paths and trekking along the edges of landslides, all to capture the fleeting silhouette of the Mountain Hawk-Eagle. As the demands of tradition and conservation pull in opposite directions, Sun joins forces with craftsman Chung Chin-nan to explore new possibilities through the creation of realistic artificial feathers.
title:香蕉天堂（數位修復版）:
1989 Golden Horse Award for Best Supporting Actor.

As the Chinese Civil War draws to a close, comrades-in-arms Men-shuan and De-sheng retreat to Taiwan with the army under assumed identities. Amidst the chaos and uncertainty of the White Terror era, the two face constant misfortune. While on the run, Men-shuan encounters a widow, Yue-xiang, and her newborn son, Yao-hua. He poses as the child's father and scrapes by, using a borrowed diploma to find work. On this "Treasure Island" famous for its bananas, a far-from-heavenly tale of absurdity and desolation unfolds, where borrowed identities unexpectedly become a lifelong reality. This is the second installment of director Wang Tung’s "Taiwan Modern Trilogy" focusing on the lives of common people, using black humor to depict the displacement and identity crises of Mainlanders adrift in Taiwan.
title:馬拉庫達大冒險:
★ Best Animation at the 2025 Silk Road International Film Festival ★ Global Box Office: 43 Million TWD ★ Directed by Victor Glukhushin, visual effects artist for *Wanted* and *Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter*.

Malakuda, the son of a tribal chief, struggles to live up to his father’s high expectations. Determined to prove his worth, he ventures alone into a primeval forest, where he unexpectedly encounters Ding-Ding, an alien bird endowed with magical powers. Together, they embark on a thrilling and whimsical adventure. However, when Ding-Ding accidentally transforms Malakuda’s father into a caterpillar, the stakes are raised. To help Ding-Ding master his magic and restore his father to his original form, Malakuda must learn to take responsibility, while his father gradually learns to let go of his sternness.
title:馬騰你別走:
(Note: Rated PG-12)
★ 2025 China Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival
★ Global Box Office: 63 Million TWD

Old Lin (Li Youbin), a retired steel mill veteran with limited mobility, lives a comfortable life but remains a perpetual "Mr. Grumpy." He crosses paths with Ma Teng (Lin Gengxin), an idle man full of useless trivia who has never quite made anything of himself. Their encounter, sparked by a botched caregiver interview, sets off a hilarious and touching journey of mutual salvation.

Mistakenly believing Ma Teng is a "killer for hire" caregiver, Old Lin hopes Ma Teng will help him end his life and draws up an "assisted suicide agreement." Ma Teng, naturally optimistic but prone to quitting everything halfway, is bold enough to chase the money but has no intention of taking a life; he only wants to earn enough to fulfill his young daughter’s small wish. Through their brief time together and an extraordinary journey, the two forge a deep bond. No longer afraid of the uncertainty of illness and death, they find a small glimmer of hope to keep moving forward.
title:魔幻開幕夜:
★ 2016 Angoulême French Film Festival ★ 2016 Brussels International Film Festival ★ Written, directed by, and starring Edouard Baer (*How to Be a Good Wife*).

With opening night looming tomorrow, theater owner Luigi finds himself facing a series of major crises tonight. To win back the respect of the renowned Japanese director Dazai, he must track down a live, performing chimpanzee. Simultaneously, he needs to secure enough funding to pay two months of overdue wages and regain the trust of his striking staff and his dependable assistant, Nawel. Along the way, he hopes to prove to his uptight and conceited intern, Faeza, that there is a different way to solve problems—one where spontaneity and fun come first! Luigi has only one night to traverse Paris, complete his mission, and save the storied Star Theater. Will he succeed against the odds, or will the curtain fail to rise on opening night?
title:魯冰花 數位修復版:
As the lupine flowers bloom, art teacher Guo Yuntian arrives in the countryside to begin his teaching post. There, he discovers Gu Aming, a mischievous boy with a vivid imagination and a natural talent for painting. Despite his family's poverty, Aming captures the world around him with an optimistic brush. But as Guo tries his best to nominate Aming for a competition, he is forced to confront the harsh and inevitable obstacles of reality.

Adapted from the novel of the same name by Zhong Zhaozheng, the "Mother of Taiwan Literature," and featuring a screenplay by Wu Nien-jen under the direction of Yang Liguo, the film views the world through the eyes of a city teacher. It captures the purity of childhood while exposing the underlying wealth gap, rigid educational systems, local politics, and rural development issues, ultimately presenting a tragedy of a life cut short. The film’s iconic theme song accompanies this tear-jerking story, speaking of longing and remaining a timeless classic.
title:（風華再現特別場）高雄有顆藍寶石: Approximately fifty years ago, Kaohsiung was home to a legendary music hall called "Sapphire." A beacon for performers and a sensation for audiences, it spearheaded the trends of the era, its influence sweeping across Taiwan and reaching as far as Southeast Asia. Local legend had it that anyone who graced the Sapphire stage would not only walk away with staggering performance fees but also see their professional status skyrocket—a true pinnacle of fame and fortune. At the time, every A-list entertainer pulled out all the stops for a chance to perform in the south, seeking the "Sapphire" coronation as the ultimate validation of their superstar status. Iconic singers such as Teresa Teng, Cui Tai-ching, Fong Fei-fei, Frankie Kao, Liu Wen-cheng, and Fei Yu-ching all graced the Sapphire stage, while legendary hosts like Chu Ke-liang, Yu Tian, and Huang Hsi-tien forged their signature performance styles within its walls.

title_norm:104歲哲代奶奶 一個人生活:
Sparking the phenomenal "Tetsuyo Craze," this heartwarming and highly-discussed film has garnered overwhelming acclaim. 

In a mountain town in Onomichi, Hiroshima, Grandma Tetsuyo Ishii lives alone in her old family home. A former elementary school teacher, she bid farewell to her husband of half a century at the age of 83. Since then, she has chosen to remain in her familiar home and community, living day by day while looking out for her niece, relatives, and neighbors.

As the years pass and the list of things she can no longer do grows, Tetsuyo continues to find clever ways to encourage herself. With a free spirit, she gradually adjusts her life to suit the present moment. This film observes Grandma Tetsuyo’s daily life from age 101 to 104, capturing not only the laughter and humor but also the inevitable goodbyes and physical pains of aging. Amidst the peaks and valleys of life, she holds onto small, meaningful rituals, proving that "living alone" does not mean being "lonely." Instead, it is a way of life—one that neither forces strength nor retreats from the world.

title_norm:2026第二季駐村藝術家聯合發表:
**2026 Season 2 Resident Artist Exhibition**

**Dates:** 2026-07-25 ~ 2026-08-09
**Venue:** Treasure Hill Artist Village

The 2026 Season 2 Resident Artist Exhibition brings together eight groups of artists from Germany, South Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Thailand, and the United States. Spanning new media, music, sound, video, installation, and cross-disciplinary media, their works examine how the passage of time and social progress continuously reshape our environment and daily lives.

**Duangjai Phuchana-Prasert** collects and experiments with soil to understand the temporal cycles of site formation. **Nicolei Buendia Gupit** utilizes ceramics and video to explore the relationship between water resources and ecology, responding to the historical water systems of Treasure Hill. **TUNALEE** draws parallels between Treasure Hill and the Sanbokdoro (mountainside roads) of Choryang-dong in Busan, South Korea, using thin layers of video and shifting light to overlay traces of war, migration, and survival.

**Kevin Corcoran** and **Jacob Sin** expand their creative focus to the connections between multiple landscapes in Northern Taiwan. Their work traces a fluid axis across historical dimensions—from the water systems of Treasure Hill, the Xindian River, and the Tamsui River to urban development, the industrial ruins of Northern Taiwan’s coal mines, and the high-tech production systems of contemporary microchip factories.

**Eunjin Liu** adopts the perspective of Taiwanese Opera, using sound installations to trace Taipei’s migration history and explore how movement shapes local identity. **Céline Ducret** draws from breathing, tides, and emotional rhythms to explore the permeable relationship between the individual and the environment. **Leo Bailly-Barton** employs interactive games to guide the audience into the symbolic order, transforming the exhibition into a space of flow, negotiation, and reorganization.

The artists invite the audience to step into their works, experiencing the mutual infiltration of history, environment, and the body through movement and stillness, and collectively sensing the "becoming" of the world.

title_norm:compact disc 記憶座標:
When an entire generation is forced to forget rather than choosing to, how can memory be preserved? Can friendship become a gentle yet persistent form of resistance? The camera follows the director and a close friend as they return to the black hole of memory; through low-key and restrained imagery, unspeakable emotions are left to ferment in the dark. More than just a documentary, this is a memorandum of youth written for one another—an exercise in collective remembering. Amidst gloomy times, through love and companionship, it pieces together a bewildered yet authentic portrait of a generation of Hong Kongers.

**2026 CPH:DOX Copenhagen International Documentary Film Festival 【Asian Premiere】**

CHAN Hau-chun｜Hong Kong｜2025｜DCP｜Colour, B&W｜29 min

A reflection on the landscapes of Hong Kong and the subtle traces left behind by its people. Within the memories of those who have left, stayed, or drifted, the film searches for intimate moments to connect one another. Blending media memories of Hong Kong’s major thoroughfares, correspondence with friends in prison, and street art, it explores the precise yet fluid moments between "presence" and "absence."

Unfolding as a tender letter, the film traces Hong Kong through its landscapes and lingering marks. Within memories of those who left, stayed, or drifted, it searches for intimate moments that quietly connect lives, attuned to the city’s subtle rhythms of change and stillness.

title_norm:future vision lab 2026:
Since 2020, the C-LAB Future Vision Lab has spearheaded the experimental exhibition project "FUTURE VISION LAB." Beginning with digital experimental architecture, the lab created the "DOME" to continuously explore the visual limits of technological media, showcasing over 200 works over the past six years. In 2023, with the support of the Ministry of Culture, the lab completed hardware and software upgrades to create the "C-LAB Dome"—Taiwan's only giant mobile outdoor immersive space with a 15-meter diameter. The immersive projection system achieves an ultra-high resolution of 8K × 8K, overcoming complex technical challenges such as calibration, stitching, alignment, playback control, and pre-production for spherical surfaces. The venue features a double-layer structure equipped with custom acoustically transparent projection membranes and a 25.4-channel surround sound environment, delivering a high-specification immersive experience. Future Vision Lab continues to optimize the creative environment of the dome to align with international standards, showcasing Taiwan’s creative energy in the field of tech-art.

"FUTURE VISION LAB 2026" will take place over eight consecutive weekends from April 18 to June 7, 2026. It brings together exceptional works from Taiwan, France, Spain, Hungary, Austria, South Korea, Japan, the USA, and Canada, featuring a total of 19 works across 16 programs. Through a diverse range of formats including exhibitions, screenings, and live performances, the festival invites audiences into the C-LAB Dome to immerse themselves in a sensory experience woven from cross-national creative intersections and diverse cultures.

title_norm:jsa共同警戒區 4k數位修復版:
The masterpiece that established director Park Chan-wook’s international reputation and became the highest-grossing South Korean film of its year, *Joint Security Area* returns for a limited 26th-anniversary 4K restored theatrical release. Through a cinematic lens that interweaves suspense and human nature, the film exposes both cruel realities and heartwarming humanity.

In the Joint Security Area (JSA) on the border between North and South Korea, two North Korean soldiers are shot dead one night under mysterious circumstances. Sophie, a Swiss-Korean female officer from a neutral nation, is dispatched to investigate the baffling case. As she peels back the layers of the investigation, she uncovers a shocking truth tied to a secret friendship that transcends national borders and historical animosity. Even as nations are pitted against each other by political hatred, a bond of brotherhood manages to cross the invisible 38th parallel. Through a seemingly casual yet precious photograph, the film conveys a profound yearning for peaceful coexistence.

His mother, Min-Min, overwhelmed by the monotony of caring for her bedridden mother, decides to seek a change. Meanwhile, his older sister Ting-Ting, a student at Taipei First Girls' High School, is navigating the restless stirrings of youth. Yang-Yang enjoys taking photos of the backs of people's heads, observing the adult world through his own lens to capture the "hidden side" that his family cannot see. In an apartment in the heart of Paris, roommates Pierre, Michel, and Jacques fully embrace their bachelorhood, living a carefree life of parties and romance. Amidst the revelry, a friend of Jacques’s sneakily asks him for a favor: to look out for an important "package" arriving the next day. Jacques agrees without a second thought, only to realize he has to leave town himself. He hastily leaves instructions for his two roommates and departs.

The next day, Pierre and Michel open the door and find themselves staring into a pair of wide, innocent eyes looking up from a cradle. They are utterly shell-shocked—how could the "package" be a baby?!

As suave as these three bachelors are in the adult world, they are completely out of their depth when it comes to caring for an infant. Director Coline Serreau masterfully uses contrast to generate humor while challenging traditional societal stereotypes regarding family roles and gendered divisions of labor. A massive box office hit in France that even outperformed *First Blood*, the film was famously remade by Hollywood as *Three Men and a Baby*.

Based on the novel *Aizen Katsura*, which has seen numerous screen adaptations, multi-talented director Cheng Tung-shan first adapted the Japanese film into a stage play before remaking it as this Taiwanese-language film starring Shi Jun and You Juan. While the original focused on a tragic romance defined by class barriers and misunderstandings, this version places greater emphasis on the silent sacrifice of maternal love and the "orphan girl" trope common in Taiwanese-language cinema. Supporting actresses Ling Ling, Chen Chiu-yen, and Cheng Hsiao-fen deliver feisty, outgoing performances as nurses, breaking the conservative gender and class constraints of the Japanese original while highlighting female friendship through humor. Additionally, the tear-jerking performance of child prodigy Hsiao Mu-lan masterfully captures the deep familial bonds central to Taiwanese melodrama.

After death and before reincarnation, departed souls arrive at a mystical realm known as "The Beyond." Here, Spirit Guardians spend their days guiding souls toward their next lives. This cycle continues until a young Spirit Guardian, Little Ghost, encounters "Little Sister," a soul who refuses to move on. Through her, the once-emotionless Little Ghost begins to see The Beyond in a completely different light.

As he attempts to lead her toward rebirth, Little Ghost uncovers the regrets of her past life. Overwhelmed by fury, Little Sister triggers an irreversible curse. If she is completely consumed by her hatred, both The Beyond and the mortal realm will be reduced to ash along with her.

Little Ghost convinces the Celestial Maiden to grant Little Sister a final chance at redemption. The Maiden dispatches the formidable warrior Heitian to accompany them on a perilous quest spanning a thousand years. Despite the constant dangers, Little Ghost repeatedly risks his own life to save her, hoping only that Little Sister can let go of her past pain, forgive herself, and finally step lightly onto the path of reincarnation.

Lord Hidetora Ichimonji, a Sengoku-era warlord who once dominated the battlefield with peerless authority, finds himself weary and aging at seventy. He decides to abdicate and divide his castles among his three sons. However, his eldest son immediately turns against him, subjecting him to humiliation and forcing him into exile. His second son also plots betrayal, treating his father with cold indifference. Only the third son—who was banished for his blunt honesty—secretly sends protection and warmly welcomes his exiled father. Witnessing the bloody fratricide of his lineage and tormented by the sins of his past, the once-mighty Hidetora descends into madness, silenced by the cruel tides of fate.

A thematic counterpart to *Kagemusha* that reaches even greater artistic heights, the film masterfully weaves Shakespeare’s tragedy *King Lear* into the Japanese Warring States period. Tatsuya Nakadai’s profound acting creates an intense emotional resonance, serving as the cornerstone of the film’s grand epic spirit. Although the production reused costumes and props from *Kagemusha*, it still cost $10 million to stage its massive battle sequences—a record-breaking budget in Japanese cinema at the time. The result is Akira Kurosawa’s ultimate masterpiece, the culmination of a lifetime of cinematic mastery.
title_norm:二百三高地:

The Meiji Restoration propelled Japan into the ranks of the world's leading powers. Its expansionist ambitions toward Northeast China and Korea provoked the Russian Empire, a traditional European power, bringing the two nations to the brink of war. To secure control over Port Arthur, the Russian army constructed what was considered the most formidable fortress in military history on the nearby "203 Hill," prepared to deliver a crushing blow to the Japanese. General Maresuke Nogi, fiercely loyal to the Emperor, led the well-equipped Third Army, determined to seize this strategic stronghold at any cost.

In a departure from his role in *Kagemusha* released that same year, Tatsuya Nakadai portrays the "War God" Nogi with restrained, commanding authority. His nuanced performance captures the crushing emotional toll of duty, a legendary portrayal that moved audiences to tears. Toei spared no expense in creating magnificent sets, enlisting Toshio Masuda—renowned for his war epics—to direct. The film’s contrast between brutal, bloody combat and the pure essence of the Bushido spirit sparked intense debate and ignited a trend for large-scale war spectacles. Following the normalization of diplomatic relations between Japan and China in 1972, Japanese films were banned from import in Taiwan; this film was screened only once during the inaugural Golden Horse International Film Exhibition in 1980 and has not been released there since.
title_norm:人生海海:

After years of working in Taiwan, Ah Yao returns to his hometown to handle his father’s funeral alongside his younger siblings. However, the proceedings are disrupted when the Religious Affairs Bureau intervenes, attempting to seize the father’s remains. In the face of this sudden conflict, the three siblings react in starkly different ways: the eldest brother, Ah Yao, chooses to yield; the younger brother, Ah Cai, opts for direct confrontation; and their sister, Shui Yun, struggles to maintain the sanctity of the ritual and order.

As the funeral progresses, long-buried family secrets begin to surface—tales of smuggling, migration, illness, and the lifelong struggle to obtain legal identification. Caught between memory and reality, the three are forced to re-examine their father and confront their own sense of belonging in this land.

In 1943, Kaji, a man driven by humanist ideals, travels with his wife Michiko to the Tiger Ridge mine in Manchuria to serve as a wartime labor supervisor. He attempts to reform the colonial system from within and improve the treatment of prisoners of war, but he is constantly marginalized by bureaucrats and pressured by the military, all while failing to win the trust of the mistreated Chinese laborers. As the machinery of war relentlessly strips away his choices, Kaji finds himself increasingly isolated. How can he protect the dignity of those around him? And how can he preserve his own conscience as a human being?

Following *Black River*, a young Tatsuya Nakadai collaborates with director Masaki Kobayashi for the second time. His righteous and restrained performance captures Kaji’s impossible dilemma, marking a major breakthrough in his acting career. This realist masterpiece, adapted from Junpei Gomikawa’s novel of the same name, stands as a pinnacle of Japanese anti-war cinema. Cinematographer Yoshio Miyajima’s static shots and black-and-white widescreen photography establish a steady, solemn visual style, grounding this cinematic epic in a cold and piercing gaze at reality.
title_norm:他們要殺你: A young woman (Zazie Beetz) must survive a night in the Vedge building, navigating a den of mysterious and twisted death traps controlled by a demonic cult, or risk becoming their next sacrifice. Produced by Andy Muschietti, the acclaimed director of the horror classic *IT*, and visionary director Kirill Sokolov, this film is an epic collision of horror, suspense, and comedy. Interweaving carnage with wicked dark humor, it makes a bold and shocking debut with its unique, wild, and alternative style.
title_norm:仲代達矢，為演員而活:
In 1975, Tatsuya Nakadai and his creative partner and wife, Kyoko Miyazaki, co-founded the acting school Mumeijuku. Nakadai personally oversees talent selection and intensive training, maintaining a rigorous schedule from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. When performing, he suppresses his own presence, allowing only the character to collide with his scene partner. Mumeijuku does more than just train actors; it cultivates "human beings" capable of standing on their own in the world, producing a steady stream of talent for 50 years. Yet, beneath his roles as a teacher and a performer, Nakadai’s true self is that of a humble actor who hand-copies his lines with a calligraphy brush and pastes them on his bedroom walls for constant memorization. 

Director Hidetaka Inozuka spent over a year following Nakadai, capturing the training process at Mumeijuku and its theatrical performances. Interspersed with interviews with Nakadai and his disciples, the film documents a side of him rarely seen by the public. At the time of filming, Nakadai was in his 80s, yet he remained steadfast on his beloved stage, battling a fading memory and declining physical strength. He continues to embrace the "beginner’s mind" of his early days as a "nobody," fulfilling his life’s mission—to live for the craft of acting—and passing this conviction on to the next generation.
title_norm:俠女數位修復版: During the Ming Dynasty, the high-ranking official Yang Lian is murdered by the eunuch Men Da of the Eastern Depot. His descendant, Yang Huizhen, along with General Shi and other members of the Donglin faction, are relentlessly pursued by the secret agent Ouyang Nian. While in hiding, Yang develops a romantic bond with the scholar Gu Shengzhai, and through Gu’s strategic brilliance, they manage to outwit and defeat their pursuers. After giving birth to a son, Huizhen secretly leaves Gu, seeking to renounce the world and enter a Buddhist monastery. As the first Chinese-language film to win an award at one of the three major European film festivals, its iconic bamboo forest duel has profoundly influenced directors such as Ang Lee, Zhang Yimou, and Tsui Hark.
title_norm:兔嘲男孩: ☀️ I hope the weather is good. See you on the rooftop.
title_norm:全面啟動: Dom Cobb is a master thief, unparalleled in the high-stakes world of corporate espionage. His specialty lies in the most dangerous and mysterious realm: the subconscious. He infiltrates the minds of his targets while they are in their most vulnerable state—deep sleep—to steal their most guarded secrets. This extraordinary talent, combined with cutting-edge technology, has made him the ultimate prize in the world of corporate intrigue, but it has come at a devastating cost. Now an international fugitive, Cobb has lost the family he loves. However, a rare opportunity for redemption arises, offering him one last chance to reclaim the life he lost.
title_norm:兩相好 數位修復版:
**2026 Udine Far East Film Festival**

Dr. Huang, a local Taiwanese practitioner of Western medicine, and Dr. Chen, a Mainlander practitioner of Traditional Chinese medicine, live next door to each other. The two families are in constant friction due to language barriers and differing customs. To make matters worse, the younger generation falls in love, escalating the neighborhood conflict and forcing everyone to reconsider the distance between them.

This film marks a pivotal turning point for director Li Hsing as he transitioned from Hokkien-language cinema to Mandarin-language cinema. It was the inaugural production of "Zili Film Company," founded by Li and his family, and served as the acting debut of Wang Man-chiao. While borrowing the comedic framework of ethnic conflict seen in Hong Kong MP&GI’s *The Greatest Civil War* series, the film shifts the root of the conflict to the misunderstandings and barriers caused by the language gap between local Taiwanese and Mainlanders. Li Hsing continues the "binary character" structure common in his Hokkien films, driving the plot through a progression from conflict to alliance. This mixed-language comedy serves as a culmination of his experience in Hokkien cinema. Notably, the film concludes with documentary footage of temple fair processions, preserving Taiwan's precious folk customs of the time in a "quasi-ethnographic" manner.

* This screening provides audio description services in Mandarin and Hokkien. Equipment is limited and prioritized for the visually impaired. If required, please visit the service counter on the 1st floor as early as possible to make a reservation. For detailed regulations, please refer to the official website.
title_norm:兩隻小鳥: A little black bird and a little white bird live together in a big tree, leading a peaceful and happy life. However, whenever something new happens, they start bickering, each trying to outdo the other. Through the simple daily lives of these two feathered protagonists, this story uses a lively and engaging way to talk to children about tolerance, jealousy, and friendship...
title_norm:公路上的遊牧人生 索: To escape domestic violence, a woman becomes a truck driver to raise her child independently. The film follows her onto the open road, delving into the male-dominated subculture of the trucking community. For these modern nomads, the highway is a way of life; traveling day and night, they face long separations from their families, poor security, labor exploitation, and health issues, sometimes relying on stimulants just to keep working. Along the way, makeshift roadside diners become vital sanctuaries for rest, connection, and solace.
title_norm:六張臉 狂言師的舞台人生:
Ninety Years on the Path of Kyogen: The Artistic Pinnacle of Living National Treasure Nomura Mansaku

Directed by Japan Academy Prize-winning director Isshin Inudo, with gentle narration by award-winning actor Joe Odagiri.

Artistry like the bright moon—profound and beyond reach.

Kyogen is a traditional Japanese performing art with a legacy spanning over 650 years, using laughter to depict the full spectrum of human emotion. A leading figure in the world of Kyogen, Living National Treasure Nomura Mansaku has dedicated himself to the craft for ninety years since his stage debut at the age of three. In 2023, he was honored with the Order of Culture. This documentary provides an intimate look at Master Nomura Mansaku as he approaches his 94th year, capturing the special occasion of his commemorative performance.

The chosen program is the classic Kyogen play *Kawakami*, a piece he has refined in recent years that poignantly explores the love between a husband and wife. The story follows a blind man who makes a pilgrimage to "Kawakami Jizo." Though his sight is miraculously restored, he is faced with a cruel trial in a dream: the deity demands that he divorce his wife. Caught between the gift of sight and the love of his life, the man faces his most agonizing decision.

Through masterful cinematography, the film not only preserves this pinnacle of performance but also captures the master’s disciplined presence backstage—the silhouette of a true craftsman in pursuit of ultimate beauty.
title_norm:再見了，可魯 數位經典重映:
In a cozy home in Tokyo, five Labrador puppies are born. One among them stands out, possessing a unique cross-shaped black birthmark on his belly and a temperament that is both gentle and intelligent. Filled with hope, his owner dreams of him becoming a guide dog for the visually impaired. Through her tireless efforts, he is eventually sent to a training center to begin his professional journey.

His name is Quill. Leaving his familiar home for the first time, he faces the first true test of his life. Under the devoted care of a foster family, Quill gradually learns to build trust and a deep bond with humans, preparing himself for rigorous training and the challenges ahead. With his innate loyalty, he will accompany Watanabe (played by Kaoru Kobayashi), a visually impaired man, through every moment of their daily lives...
title_norm:冷戰認知敘事 系列座談ｉ 黃立慧 時間的女兒 中的 誤讀:
**Time:** Friday, July 10, 2026 | 19:30–21:30
**Location:** Multi-function Room 303, CREATORS Space, Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB) (No. 177, Sec. 1, Jianguo S. Rd., Da’an Dist., Taipei City)
**Panelists:** Huang Li-hui (Artist), Wu Ssu-feng (Theater Critic), Chen Wei-chien (Art Critic)
**Moderator:** Chang Tsung-kun (PhD Student, Institute of Social Research and Cultural Studies, NYCU)

### ▍Talk Introduction
"Since she was a child, Li-hui felt that Ying-wu was different from others."

It all began with a "misreading": a father’s ideology and political beliefs were misidentified, leading to interrogation and imprisonment—a process that continues to this day, consolidated and institutionalized by historical archives, commemorations, and interpretations. Ying-wu repeatedly instructed Li-hui: "Don't get the general direction wrong." In an era where history has become a "struggle between memory and memory," what exactly is "correct"? How can one begin to unpack this without falling into further misreading? If "misreading" triggered the creation of *The Daughter of Time* years ago, then as the work enters the battlefield of discourse, how should we read—or resist misreading—once more? How do we navigate a path of practice through constant calibration and escape?

Since 2017, artist Huang Li-hui has been developing her *Family Soap Opera* series, which focuses on identifying how historical and national narratives are formed and circulated through the "family"—the fundamental unit of society—in the post-Cold War era. As the artist immerses herself in the creation of the series' finale, *910 Highview*, during her residency, this lecture series will trace the ten-year trajectory of *Family Soap Opera*. By examining individual works, the talks will re-evaluate the political and artistic contexts they inhabit to reflect on the positioning and strategy of her new work.

This retrospective also aims to confront the prevailing trends in art related to the White Terror and transitional justice that have emerged alongside this series. The lecture situates this historical background within the problem of "Cold War cognitive narratives," using three sub-themes—"Misreading," "Translation" (July 25), and "Artificiality" (August 11)—as clues. These correspond respectively to the series' sequential releases: *The Daughter of Time* (2017), *My Mother is a Good German* (2020), and *Alpinia B-side* (2021). The talk will further explore the historical environments behind these works and the Cold War concepts—or contemporary reflections—mirrored through generational sensibilities.

---

### ▍Artist Profile
**♦︎ Huang Li-hui**
A full-time artist, Huang holds an MFA in Art and Design from National Taipei University of Education (2008) and an MFA in Performance Art from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago (2013). Her work often stems from personal dilemmas, exploring the boundaries between individuals and collectives. She seeks to find the intersection between grand narratives and personal histories to expand the perceptual dimensions of her subjects. Her media include performance, video, and installation, with a particular focus on the temporal correspondence between live performance and documentary traces. Her decade-long series *Family Soap Opera* explores the gaps in collective narratives. She has been nominated for the 19th and 20th Taishin Arts Awards, and her work has been exhibited in Taiwan, the US, Germany, and Mexico.

---

### ▍Panelist Profiles
**♦︎ Wu Ssu-feng**
A theater critic and editor based in Hualien/Taitung. He participates in theater primarily through writing and editing, as well as curation and production.

**♦︎ Chen Wei-chien**
Currently a teacher of contemporary art for amateurs (Director of "Fat Teacher" Painting and Photography Studio) and an art critic. He served as a contributing critic for the Taishin Bank Foundation for Arts and Culture (2013–2024). His writings appear in *Artco*, *Artist Magazine*, and other media. He is the author of *Taiwan Photographers Series: Quo Ying-sheng* (2019). He is dedicated to contemporary art and hopes to make it more accessible through writing and teaching.

---

### ▍Moderator Profile
**♦︎ Chang Tsung-kun**
A PhD student at the Institute of Social Research and Cultural Studies, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University. His research interests span the Cold War, infrastructure, and labor, with a focus on historical representation and its politics within the arts. His art criticism can be found in the *Performing Arts Review*, *PAR Magazine*, *ARTouch*, and *CLABO*.

---

**Further Reading:**
*   Introduction to *The Daughter of Time*
*   Wang Sheng-hung, "Historical Hardship at the Other End of the Lever: A Short Review of Huang Li-hui’s Solo Exhibition 'The Daughter of Time'"
*   Chen Wei-zhen, "Using Nothingness as Being, Lightness as Weight: Huang Li-hui’s 'The Daughter of Time'"
*   Chen Wei-chien, "Huang Li-hui’s Solo Exhibition 'The Daughter of Time'"
*   Huang Hai-ming, "So Close Yet So Far: Reading 'The Daughter of Time' at Haiton Art Center"
*   Introduction to the *910 HIGHVIEW* Project

**Lecture Curators:** Huang Li-hui, Tung Yung-wei
**Organizer:** Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB), CREATORS Creation/Research Support Program

title_norm:切腹:
1962 Kinema Junpo Top 10 Japanese Films (3rd Place)
1963 Cannes Film Festival Special Jury Prize
1963 Blue Ribbon Awards for Best Actor & Best Screenplay

In 1630 (the seventh year of the Kanei era), the centralized rule of the third Tokugawa Shogun, Iemitsu, weakened the power of the daimyo houses, leaving once-proud samurai to wander as masterless ronin. During this time, many ronin began extorting money from daimyo estates by threatening to commit ritual suicide (seppuku) on their grounds—a nuisance that plagued many, including the prestigious Ii clan. One day, an elderly ronin named Tsugumo Hanshiro arrives at the Ii estate, requesting a place to commit seppuku. The clan's retainers decide to call his bluff, intending to force him to follow through with the act. However, as the old man slowly recounts the story of his journey, his true intentions are gradually revealed.

Following *The Human Condition*, Tatsuya Nakadai and Masaki Kobayashi collaborate once again. Based on Yasuhiko Takiguchi's novel *Ibun Ronin-ki* and written by legendary screenwriter Shinobu Hashimoto, the film employs a non-linear narrative to build a masterful atmosphere of suspense. Captured by cinematographer Yoshio Miyajima, known for his grand visual scale, the film depicts a tragic and brutal tale of revenge. In an era and nation that glorified the code of Bushido, this film offers a bold and scathing critique—a spirit that Tatsuya Nakadai has frequently praised, citing this as one of his favorite works.
title_norm:刺蠻王:
The swordsman Jin Shange originally intended to serve his country by joining the ranks of Marshal Zhang Zhe. However, he was framed for the murder of the Prime Minister's son and sentenced to exile at the frontier. During his transport, the escort was ambushed by Jin soldiers; in the chaos, Jin Shange broke free from his shackles, defeated the enemy, and escaped.

Meanwhile, Marshal Zhang Zhe was killed by the Jin commander, Wanyan. The Marshal's daughter, Enzhu, managed to flee to Lu Village with the help of Wang Feng. Seeking vengeance, they began recruiting heroes to their cause. Jin Shange happened to pass by their martial arts tournament, where his peerless skills impressed Wang Feng, who invited him to join the resistance against the Jin invaders. Jin Shange readily agreed, but on one condition: he must marry Enzhu. To avenge her father, Enzhu consented, provided that Jin Shange first return with Wanyan’s head.

Jin Shange initially presents himself as a decadent, roguish, and even lecherous figure, subverting the traditional "chivalrous hero" archetype of wuxia cinema. As the group unites to fight the Jin, this unconventional warrior gradually redeems his image, ultimately making a stylish, solitary exit reminiscent of a classic Western hero.
title_norm:劇場版 暗殺教室 我們的時光: It is a day in late February; exams have ended, and graduation is just around the corner. Under the government’s increasingly strict surveillance, the students of Class 3-E look back on the year they spent with Koro-sensei. Memories flood back—the washable tattoo graffiti they drew on Ms. Bitch, the special swimming lessons, the rivalry with Class A, and Valentine’s Day chocolates—filling the classroom with nostalgic laughter and chatter. Meanwhile, despite being hunted by a quartet of assassins during winter break, Koro-sensei evaded them with his usual effortless ease.
title_norm:動物哇哈哈 斑馬好忙: A work by German animation director Julia Ocker, this short animated comedy features a minimalist visual style and brisk pacing. Unique and full of humor, it is a lighthearted and delightful experience.
