title_norm:北美館開放網絡計畫 │藝術家座談安娜・里德勒 x 白其薇:
**[Artist Talk] Browsing the Site | Every Iris on the Internet (The First 100,000)**

**Time:** Thursday, May 21, 2026 ‧ UTC+8 20:00–21:30
**Location:** Online Talk
**Speaker:** Anna Ridler
**Discussant:** Clara Che Wei Peh
**Moderator:** Huang Xiang-yun
**Registration:** Please visit the exhibition page for *The Reaction of Disappearance* (click this link).
The online link for this event will be emailed to registrants two days prior (May 19). The 90-minute session will include consecutive interpretation (Mandarin/English) and a Q&A session, conducted bilingually.

**About the Talk**
Artist Anna Ridler, joined by discussant Clara Che Wei Peh, will lead the audience through a live online browsing of her work *Every Iris on the Internet (The First 100,000)* (2025). During this guided tour, the two will discuss the commonalities in their artistic practices and research methodologies. They will explore how this work reflects their shared research interests: deconstructing how data is enshrined as a modern myth, speculatively reimagining the futures of history and ecology, and examining how intricate systems of control shape both human and non-human worlds.

**Speaker | Anna Ridler**
Anna Ridler is an artist and researcher whose work explores systems of knowledge and how technology is invented and used to understand the world, particularly the natural world. Her practice often begins with data collection, using datasets to develop strange new narratives. Her work has been exhibited at numerous major international cultural institutions, including Times Square (New York), the Barbican Centre (London), Centre Pompidou (Paris), HeK (House of Electronic Arts, Basel), The Photographers' Gallery (London), ZKM Center for Art and Media (Karlsruhe), Ars Electronica (Linz), and the Victoria and Albert Museum (London). She was selected by *Artnet* as one of nine "pioneer artists" exploring the creative potential of AI and was nominated for a Golden Nica in the "Artificial Intelligence & Life Art" category at Ars Electronica in 2019.

**Discussant | Clara Che Wei Peh**
Clara Che Wei Peh is a curator and art critic based in Singapore. As the founder of Common Protocol, she is dedicated to promoting new media art practices in Southeast Asia. She also initiated Monday Chatroom, a touring discussion series focused on issues at the intersection of art and technology. Her curatorial projects have been presented at institutions such as The Institutum, ArtScience Museum, and DECK Photography Art Centre. Previously, she served as the Public Programmes Curator for the Asymmetry Art Foundation, an Asian Collections Researcher for the KADIST Art Foundation, Curator of the Digital section at Art Dubai, and an adjunct lecturer at LASALLE College of the Arts. Her research and criticism have appeared in the *Asian Art Biennial Reader*, *ArtAsiaPacific*, *The Brooklyn Rail*, and *Art and Market*. Currently, she is a member of The Lumen Prize International Selectors Committee and has served as a nominator for the LG Guggenheim Award and an external reviewer for SIGGRAPH Asia. You can follow her on Instagram: @claralikesart.

**Moderator | Huang Xiang-yun**
Huang Xiang-yun is a researcher in the philosophy of art and a visual artist. Her research focuses on post-colonialism, cyberfeminism, digital materialism, and critical AI theory, exploring the relationship between the "body" and "technology" through these lenses. She has curated exhibitions and performances including the online exhibition *Stuck? Click Me* (in collaboration with Aksioma, Slovenia, and KUNSTSURFER, Switzerland), *www.reverse-database.commons* at the Taipei Fine Arts Museum, *Our Terms, Our Conditions* at the IMPAKT Festival, *Fragments of Truth* at the Taipei Digital Art Festival, and the *Body Interface Project*. Her dance films and performance videos often stem from her own poetry, exploring the vulnerability of (non)human existence, collective mourning, and digital intimacy. Her work has been supported by the Mondriaan Fund (Netherlands) through the "New Artist Grant" and the National Culture and Arts Foundation (Taiwan). Her works have been exhibited at MOCA Taipei, the Cinedans Festival & Eye Filmmuseum (Netherlands), the Museum of Contemporary Art Belgrade, Ars Electronica, the Kikk Festival (Belgium), and panke.gallery (Berlin).

title_norm:南北一家親:
Food is the soul of the people, but for two portly rivals, the dining table is a battlefield. In the 1960s, Leung Sing-po, owner of a Cantonese restaurant, and Liu En-chia, who runs a Northern-style eatery, resort to every trick imaginable to steal each other's business, bringing the deep-seated cultural differences between North and South to the surface. To their horror, their children fall in love, sending the two fathers into a rage. The feud escalates from verbal sparring to full-blown fisticuffs, with "Shadowless Kicks" and "Mount Tai Presses" flying, eventually forcing the young couple to stage a fake elopement. Can the two fathers set aside their prejudices for their children’s sake and turn their rivalry into friendship?

Following the massive success of the 1961 film *The Greatest Civil War* (directed by Wong Tin-lam and written by Stephen Soong), MP & GI struck while the iron was hot the following year. Producer Stephen Soong invited Golden Horse-winning screenwriter Chin Yu to provide the original story and commissioned the legendary Eileen Chang to pen the screenplay. Infusing MP & GI’s signature warmth with a slapstick energy, Chang crafted a vibrant North-South comedy rich in local wit and cultural clashes.
title_norm:原鄉人數位修復客語版: Writer Zhong Li-he falls in love with Zhong Ping-mei, but because they share the same surname, their relationship faces fierce opposition from their families. It is only through Ping-mei’s unwavering support and care that he is able to spend his sleepless nights pursuing his literary dreams on manuscript paper. The film’s theme song, performed by Teresa Teng, further resonates with the hearts of the public.

At the same time, a new facial recognition technology is being tested. Conan receives a call from Subaru Okiya, informing him that an Interpol agent has been murdered in Germany by Gin. title_norm:向世界說聲嗨 歐亞河貍: Did you know that Eurasian beavers are the "underwater architects" of the wetlands? Born in the spring, beaver kits learn to swim within a month and store food underwater before winter arrives. By building dams, they alter water currents and enrich the wetland ecosystem. Once driven to the brink of extinction by hunting, they are now protected but still face the ongoing challenges of river development. This is a story about family and coexistence with the environment. *Say Hi to the World* is both an animated documentary and a narrative short film that uses an innovative, unconventional approach to tell the stories of various animals' births and lives.
title_norm:呼吸練習:
★ Official Selection, 46th Golden Harvest Awards

That summer, Mother was hospitalized once again. Yi-ling felt adrift, burdened by the secrets of her birth and the sudden, inexplicable jealousy of her older sister, Si-qing. Through the repetition of daily life, they practice breathing with all their might, while learning to face the day that death inevitably arrives.
title_norm:哈姆奈特: England, 1580. William Shakespeare, a struggling Latin tutor, meets the free-spirited Agnes. Deeply drawn to one another, they embark on a passionate romance and quickly marry, building a happy life with their three children. However, as William’s theatrical career flourishes in distant London, Agnes is left to anchor their home alone. When a sudden tragedy strikes, the couple’s once-unbreakable bond is pushed to its limits—an experience that would eventually inspire Shakespeare’s immortal masterpiece, *Hamlet*.
title_norm:喀布爾，信仰之間:
Amidst the echoes of prayer and rifles slung over shoulders, faith and weaponry define the everyday. Two devout Afghan brothers live within this world: the elder patrols his post, dreaming of martyrdom while burdened by mundane worries; the younger, still a child, spends his days herding, playing, and reciting scripture, looking up to his brother with an innocence written across his face. Eschewing judgment for an open lens, the film offers a microscopic look at the coming-of-age of males under Taliban theocracy. What outsiders perceive as indoctrination is, to them, a sense of fulfillment and redemption, leaving the audience caught between empathy and profound shock.

title_norm:地獄新娘 數位修復版:
Upon hearing that her sister has drowned, Rui-mei, an overseas Chinese woman, returns to Taiwan in secret. Concealing her true identity, she moves into her brother-in-law’s home as a tutor for her niece, determined to uncover the truth behind the tragedy. As they spend their days together, she not only helps mend the fractured bond between father and daughter but also finds herself falling for her brother-in-law. Amidst the shadows of a haunted mansion, the discovery of a secret diary, and a web of tangled emotions, the truth slowly begins to emerge. But just as her brother-in-law proposes, a deadly conspiracy erupts on the eve of their wedding.

Drawing inspiration from the Brontë sisters and Daphne du Maurier, British author Victoria Holt rose to fame in 1960 with her Gothic romance *Mistress of Mellyn*. After its serialization in Taiwanese newspapers and subsequent publication by Crown Press, the novel ignited a craze for Western romance across the island. Director Hsin Chi masterfully transplants the British suspense and romance of the original novel into the local atmosphere of Tamsui. With sophisticated staging and cinematography, the film not only demonstrates high production standards but also proves that Taiwanese filmmakers were capable of far more than just tragic melodramas—showcasing their ability to master international genres and literary adaptations with a diverse creative vision.
title_norm:地球迷航:
★ 2021 Golden Horse Film Festival

People with autism are naturally unable to understand or learn conventional ways of expressing emotion, making it difficult for them to navigate the complex social interactions of mainstream society. However, they often fixate on specific interests, demonstrating unique talents in fields such as painting, music, and writing. For over a decade, teacher Han Shu-hua has taught painting to individuals with autism, constantly amazed by the unique aesthetic styles of these "stars in the daytime." In 2003, she founded the Duo Bao Art School to provide a creative sanctuary for adults on the autism spectrum. Director Lin Cheng-sheng has been documenting their daily lives since then. Through intimate observation of four individuals, the film explores their interactions with peers, family, and teachers, revealing a unique state of existence and an innate emotional language that differs from the world at large.

It is there that Moussa promises to accompany Rosie to visit her father, who is currently in prison. An extension of the artwork *Mound* from the "Building a Park" project, this performance responds to the history of Yuanshan Park and its prehistoric shell mound ruins. Artist Yang Yu-chiao joins sound artist Chiang Hsin-wei to present a unique collaborative experience. Through storytelling, AI-assisted experimental video, and the physical traces left by audience members throwing chalk and live writing, the performance acts as an archaeological "excavation" of actions and marks, echoing the layers of memory accumulated over time.

**【About the Artwork: *Mound*】**
*Mound* uses "play" as a metaphor for understanding human civilization. The traces left by daily activities accumulate over time, eventually transforming into historical ruins that can be traced back. The work is inspired by the various architectural eras of Yuanshan Park and the cultural remains unearthed at the Yuanshan Archaeological Site—including stone tools, wooden implements, and post-hole clusters—pointing to the "accumulations" formed by human life.

Artist Yang Yu-chiao utilizes the physical properties of chalk and blackboards, inviting the audience to participate through the playful act of throwing. As chalk rolls and collides across the surface, it leaves randomly generated traces, much like sounds that once existed but have since faded. Ultimately, the chalk accumulates in a collection bin to be "excavated" and revealed during the artist's performance, allowing the audience to re-examine the layers of time and memory generated by collective action.

title_norm:家庭檔案影像的轉生與收納:
Every household has a collection of once-popular audiovisual media—16mm and 8mm film, VHS tapes, DVs, and DVDs—that hold family memories, event recordings, and personal histories. However, in an era where playback equipment is increasingly hard to find, digitizing these formats seems to be the only way to ensure they can be easily viewed and remembered.

In addition to introducing how these formats can be converted into digital files, this event will explore the differences in presentation and preservation between digital files and original media. We will also discuss the potential for building a personal archive through the process of collecting and converting these materials. 16mm and 8mm projectors will be available on-site; participants are welcome to bring their own films if they wish.

Every path of wandering leads to an unknown, beautiful encounter that sparks the imagination. You are cordially invited to join "The Shrewd Observer" for an Art Promenade—a journey of wonder through the exhibition.

**Time:** Saturday, August 1, 2026 | 14:00–15:30
**Speaker:** Shih Wei-chu | Associate Professor, Department of French, National Central University
**Venue:** Exhibition Rooms D, E, and F, Basement Level
**Meeting Point:** 13:55 in front of the Misty Garden, Basement Level
**Registration:** Online reservation required. Limited to 30 participants. Registration opens July 15 at 10:30 AM.

**Reminders:**
The event is free, but participants must purchase a museum admission ticket and comply with the museum’s bag storage regulations. This activity is recommended for teenagers (junior high and above) and adults. As the tour involves walking and standing within the galleries, please wear comfortable shoes and consider your physical stamina before participating. Registered guests should complete check-in between 13:30 and 13:55; late arrivals will have their spots released to on-site waitlisted visitors.

**Introduction:**
The "Art Promenade" is a creative extension of the traditional expert-led gallery tour. It invites experts and scholars from the art world and various interdisciplinary fields to respond to exhibitions through their unique expertise and creativity. By offering non-traditional modes of appreciation and interpretation, these guides share fresh perspectives with the audience.

For the first generation of Surrealist creators, cinema offered expansive technical possibilities. Through editing, superimposition, collage, and various experimental techniques, they were able to subvert reality, abolish natural laws and logic through fiction, and create absurd, hallucinatory visual effects. In this medium, objects, spaces, and bodies undergo various metamorphoses, carrying diverse symbolic meanings—making film a powerful new vehicle for conveying their creative philosophies.

Today, surreal cinematic plots and imagery have become commonplace for contemporary audiences. This promenade adopts an open, informal approach, inviting the audience to become "Shrewd Observers." Together with speaker Shih Wei-chu, participants will explore selected film segments, images, and the anecdotes behind them, while tracing the marks of Surrealism within contemporary Taiwanese cinema.

**Keywords:** #The Razor that Slices Reason #The Dog that Never Appeared

**About the Speaker:**
Shih Wei-chu is an Associate Professor in the Department of French at National Central University and the former Director of the Taiwan Film Research Center. Her research interests include the history and culture of moving images, small-gauge film history, film aesthetics, contemporary visual arts, and image education. She also served as the co-curator for "The Untitled Volume: Small-Gauge Amateur Films and Others" at the 14th Taiwan International Documentary Festival (2024).

Instead, she finds herself thrust into the next stage of the nightmare. This time, her long-estranged sister, Faith (Kathryn Newton), is caught in the crossfire. Grace has one shot to survive, protect her sister, and seize "The High Seat"—the council that rules the world. Hunted by four rival families vying for the throne, only one will emerge to claim ultimate power.
title_norm:弟弟追著恐龍跑:
★ 2020 European Film Academy Young Audience Award
★ 2020 Italian Silver Ribbon Award Nomination for Best New Director
★ 2020 David di Donatello Awards: David of the Youth; Best Actress Nomination

Jack’s younger brother, Gio, has Down syndrome. As a child, Jack believed his parents' lie that Gio was a child with superpowers, just like in the comic books. However, now that Jack is starting high school, he no longer believes his brother is a superhero. In fact, he finds him embarrassing, especially after meeting Elena. Jack refuses to let himself be humiliated in front of the girl of his dreams, and caring for his brother soon becomes a burden. Jack even goes as far as pretending he doesn't have a brother, hiding the truth from his new classmates and especially from Elena. But if you cannot love someone for everything they are, including their flaws, others will never love you for everything you are. Through his direct nature, unique perspective, and simple yet wise words, Gio will teach his brother Jack this essential life lesson.
title_norm:影城介紹:
★ Based on the true story of a guide dog's life! Relive the heartwarming animal cinema classic that moved millions.
★ A rare exploration of the guide dog theme, using a delicate narrative to sincerely portray the profound bond between humans and dogs.
★ A nuanced portrayal of the challenges faced by the visually impaired, witnessing the emotional journey from initial resistance to ultimate trust.

Five adorable Labrador puppies are born into a Tokyo household. One stands out from the rest, marked by a unique cross-shaped black birthmark on its belly. Since the puppies' father was a guide dog, their owner harbors a long-held hope that one of them will follow in his footsteps and become an exceptional guide dog. Because the mother was not a guide dog, the owner’s requests are repeatedly rejected. Undeterred, her persistence finally pays off when a trainer from a guide dog school reluctantly agrees to take one of the puppies for a trial. The puppy with the birthmark is the one chosen, marking the very first separation of its life.

Movie Trailer
title_norm:影武者:
1980 Cannes Film Festival – Palme d'Or
1981 Mainichi Film Awards – Best Film, Director, Actor, Art Direction, and Music
1981 Academy Awards – Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film and Best Art Direction

During the height of Japan’s Sengoku period, the formidable warlord Takeda Shingen dominates the land with his brilliant leadership, only to be unexpectedly shot on the battlefield. On his deathbed, he orders his inner circle to keep his passing a secret to maintain morale and deter his rivals. Desperate to maintain order, his retainers recruit a common criminal who bears a striking resemblance to Shingen to serve as his "Kagemusha" (Shadow Warrior). As the political landscape shifts like the wind, enemies surround them like a forest, and war rages like fire, can this double embody Shingen’s tiger-like majesty and remain as immovable as a mountain while commanding the clan?

Early in production, Akira Kurosawa clashed with the original lead actor, leading Tatsuya Nakadai to step in at the last minute to play both Takeda Shingen and the Shadow Warrior. His nuanced performance, seamlessly shifting between the aura of a legendary general and the coarseness of a commoner, helped Kurosawa secure the Palme d'Or and served as a precursor to their collaboration on *Ran*. This epic production nearly collapsed due to a lack of funding, but was saved when renowned directors George Lucas and Francis Ford Coppola stepped in to help secure international financing—a story that has since become legendary in the film world.
title_norm:心聆舞曲:
★ 2025 Jussi Award Nomination for Best Breakthrough Performance
★ The latest film from Jenni Toivoniemi, director of *Force of Habit*

In the heat of the Finnish summer, 29-year-old Sili and her optimistic father, Petri, find themselves in a clash of perspectives at a tango festival. Sili is a habitual "no," while Petri is a perpetual "yes." Their polar-opposite personalities lead to a constant stream of misunderstandings and mishaps; while Sili is preoccupied with managing her boss's marital crisis, Petri masks his inner turmoil, using the elegance of the tango to maintain a facade of normalcy. As the final dance comes to an end, cold reality forces them to finally confront the lies they’ve been telling each other.
title_norm:恨 30週年4k修復版: Adapted from true events and set in the 18th arrondissement of 1990s Paris, a neighborhood home to many Middle Eastern and African immigrant communities as well as various gangs. In a place where volatile clashes between police and residents have become a daily reality, a riot breaks out. Vinz, a young Jewish man, is left fuming after his close friend is brutally beaten by police and hospitalized. Having accidentally found a service revolver lost in the chaos, Vinz and his friends begin searching for a chance to exact their revenge on the world.
title_norm:惡女花魁:
The directorial debut of Japanese photography icon Mika Ninagawa returns to the big screen. 

Sold to the Tamagiku-ya house in Yoshiwara at the age of eight, young Kiyoha begins her journey in the world of courtesans. Naturally rebellious and fiercely competitive, she flourishes under the mentorship of the high-ranking Shohi, eventually growing into a dazzling beauty who commands every eye in the room. Navigating a decadent world of luxury and vice, Kiyoha defies the traditional submissiveness of her peers, instead using her "cool and aloof" persona as the ultimate weapon to captivate men. As the years pass, she follows the same path as those before her—weathering heartbreak, disillusionment, and wild abandon—until she finally ascends to the rank of Oiran, the supreme courtesan of Yoshiwara.

Yet, just as she reaches the pinnacle of her career, an unforgettable shower of cherry blossoms alters her destiny once more, leading to a rebellious final choice that leaves everyone stunned. 

Based on the manga by Moyoco Anno, with music directed by J-rock queen Sheena Ringo and starring the iconic Anna Tsuchiya, this film is an explosive showcase of female creative power—a true feast for both the eyes and ears.
title_norm:愛在日落巴黎時: Nine years later, they reunite in Paris. Jesse has turned their brief encounter in Vienna into a bestselling novel, and today he is in the city for a book signing. Having seen the news, Celine arrives at the event. With only about 90 minutes before Jesse must depart for the United States, the two—who have since built separate lives—share a coffee and wander through the romantic backstreets of Paris, eventually boarding a boat on the Seine as the sun begins to set. Their conversation shifts from guarded, prideful exchanges to slowly letting their defenses down once again...
title_norm:愛染桂:
2009 Tokyo FILMeX IFF. Kozo, the young heir to a hospital, meets the nurse Katsue at a banquet. Beneath a katsura tree at a temple, they pledge their eternal love, unaware that Katsue is hiding a difficult past as a young widow with a small daughter. The two plan to elope to Kyoto, but Katsue is forced to miss their rendezvous at the last moment when her daughter falls ill. Misunderstandings and regrets soon drive them apart. As Katsue eventually finds her footing through her musical talent, will these two lost lovers ever find their way back to each other?

Based on Matsutaro Kawaguchi’s novel of the same name, this film was a massive hit in Japan and was also deeply beloved by Taiwanese audiences during the colonial era. It went on to profoundly influence the melodramatic conventions of post-war Taiwanese-language cinema, and its classic theme song, "Tabi no Yokaze" (Night Wind of Travel), is still sung today. Although the film spawned numerous sequels and remakes, the original 1938 full-length version of *The Love-Troth Tree* (Parts I and II) is tragically lost. Only a "digest" version, re-edited at the time of its release, remains. While the narrative may feel somewhat fragmented, Kinuyo Tanaka’s delicate and nuanced performance remains profoundly moving even after all these years.
title_norm:感官世界 數位修復版: Abe Sada, a tavern waitress and former celebrated geisha, enters into an illicit affair with her married employer, Kichizo Ishida. They seize every spare moment for secret trysts, meeting in nearby rooms or secluded hideaways. As her feelings intensify, Sada finds the existence of Kichizo’s wife increasingly unbearable. Once their affair is exposed, she becomes consumed by the realization that her lover’s body does not belong to her alone. Faced with a reality they cannot change, the two descend into a world of their own, surrendering to a frenzy of carnal desire. Indulging their sexual instincts and racing toward the death drive, they push the boundaries of eroticism to the limit, finally achieving a state of absolute possession.
title_norm:我們的6e班:
(Note: Rated PG-12) Starring Eric Suen and Alex Fong.

In Hong Kong, there is an unconventional "international school" called Inspirational Secondary School. The student body is primarily composed of South Asian youths, alongside new immigrants from Mainland China and local students with poor academic performance. Due to behavioral issues and a lack of educational support, the atmosphere between teachers and students has long been fraught with tension. To foster a sense of belonging and break down racial barriers, Park Sir (Eric Suen) and Miss Law (Yip Tsz-yu) look to the annual inter-school talent competition, hoping to teach the students of Class 6E the value of teamwork. However, just as rehearsals are in full swing, several students begin to face a series of unexpected challenges...
title_norm:我只是個士兵:
At the outbreak of the Russo-Ukrainian War, the director volunteered to enlist to document the battlefield firsthand, but military life proved far more difficult to adapt to than he had imagined. As the conflict ground into a stalemate, the bloodshed, cruelty, and isolation began to erode his sensibilities as a chronicler. When death claims loved ones and comrades, leaving only the spread of hatred and rendering life as cheap as weeds, is humanity spread too thin to find a place to dwell? Once one becomes a machine that pulls the trigger without hesitation, is it possible to reclaim the once-familiar comforts of love and family?

Filmed over three and a half years on Ukraine’s frontline, the film follows a young filmmaker who trades his camera for a rifle and joins the Territorial Defence Forces. As war reshapes his life, he moves from storyteller to soldier, documenting fear, loss, and resilience amid chaos.

2025 Sheffield Doc/Fest
2025 Toronto IFF

title_norm:我可能不會變瘦:
★ 2011 SCHLiNGEL International Film Festival: Best International Feature Film, Best European Children's Film
★ 2011 Netherlands Film Festival: Best Production Design
★ 2011 Rembrandt Awards: Nominated for Best Dutch Film and Best Dutch Actress

Dik Trom is a lively and cheerful boy who is as honest as he is chubby. However, his happy life is turned upside down when he and his family move to Thin Town. His father opens a restaurant there, but the locals rarely dine out, and there isn't a single overweight person in sight. When Dik falls for Lieve, the thinnest girl in town, he does everything in his power to win her over and show the townspeople the true beauty that lies within.
title_norm:我在荒野做了一場夢: Explorer Hsu Jen-hsiu has spent 50 years traversing the wild rainforests, documenting the majesty and fragility of nature through his lens and writings. He is more than just an observer; he is a traveler who lives in harmony with the natural world. However, in 2019, he underwent his first surgery—a warning from his body that time was catching up. This sparked what he calls his "Final Adventure," a journey deep into the Amazon in pursuit of the Blue Morpho butterfly, a dream he has held for many years.
title_norm:我家哞哞叫:
Edgar leads a quiet, solitary life. A dedicated foodie, he visits a slaughterhouse one day and unexpectedly witnesses the birth of a calf. Moved by compassion, he begins a new life living with the calf and even turns vegetarian! However, his new roommate soon turns his world upside down—knocking over the TV, smashing lamps, and even shattering a glass jar full of spare change. Pushed to his breaking point, Edgar begins sharpening his knives. What will be the calf’s fate? Featuring a cynical middle-aged man and an adorable calf, this film is the ultimate display of "odd-couple" charm!

Tickets for all screenings for the following month become available on the 25th of each month at 9:00 AM. Each person is limited to 4 tickets per screening.
title_norm:我的對手是隻鵝:
The battle between boy and goose is about to begin! A young boy dreaming of becoming a soccer player is practicing in his backyard one day when a temperamental goose suddenly appears, turning his life upside down. It seems that before he can achieve his dreams, our hero must first get past the "goose"! 

Beneath its humorous and quirky plot lies a touching story of family bonds. This witty 3D puppet animation is sure to leave you with a wide smile and plenty to savor long after you leave the theater.
title_norm:托斯卡尼艷陽下: Frances, a writer reeling from a recent divorce, travels to Tuscany, Italy, at the encouragement of her best friend. What was meant to be a simple getaway takes an unexpected turn when, through a twist of fate, she impulsively buys a crumbling villa named "Bramasole." Dilapidated and overgrown, the house is a reflection of her own fractured life. Frances decides to stay and restore the villa herself. Throughout the renovation, she encounters eccentric yet warm-hearted neighbors, a group of spirited workers, and countless unexpected surprises.
title_norm:抓馬戀人: Charlie met Emma at a cafe, where a clumsy icebreaker sparked a two-year romance. Just as the two were convinced they had found "the one" and began planning their wedding, a gathering with friends turned their world upside down. During a game of "sharing your worst past," Emma unexpectedly confesses a shocking secret from her history. The revelation leaves everyone in disbelief and forces Charlie to re-examine their entire relationship. On the verge of walking down the aisle, their love faces a grueling test of honesty and trust.
title_norm:捕風追影:
A heist of the century has shocked the city! The "Shadow Group," a gang of genius thieves, has made off with hundreds of millions in assets. Utilizing elite counter-surveillance skills, they managed to escape unscathed, making a mockery of the police's "Sky Eye" surveillance system. 

With the investigation at a standstill, the Macau Judiciary Police recall retired surveillance expert Huang Dezhong (Jackie Chan). Huang mentors young officer He Qiuguo (Zhang Zifeng) and others to reform the "Secret Surveillance Unit," eventually narrowing their sights on the mastermind behind the gang—the "Wolf King," Fu Longsheng (Tony Leung Ka-fai). But as the police lay an inescapable dragnet, the Shadow Group deploys a genius hacker (Ci Sha) and their tactical leader (Wen Junhui) to set a perfect trap within a trap...
title_norm:改造音痴妹:
Starring Park Ha-sun (winner of the MBC Entertainment Awards Sitcom Excellence Award for *Dong Yi*) and Yoon Sang-hyun (*Secret Garden*).

Dong-joo inherited her "zero musical sense" from her mother, who runs a mung bean pancake shop. To make matters worse, her singing voice sounds strangely androgynous. Unable to bear the constant ridicule for being tone-deaf any longer, she decides to seek professional help.

Short on both time and money, Dong-joo discovers "Dr. Voice Tone-Deaf Clinic," a facility that claims to cure the tone-deaf using scientific methods and systematic training. Seeing them as her only savior, Dong-joo poses as a high school student to enroll in an intensive course at the half-price student rate.

The clinic is filled with all sorts of patients—from those who can't hit a note or keep a beat to those with absolutely no rhythm. However, Dong-joo turns out to be a far more hopeless case than any of them. Shin-heung, the clinic’s star instructor, is an unremarkable-looking man with a bit of a body odor problem. After taking on a "special grade" tone-deaf student like Dong-joo, he fears his professional reputation is at stake. Forced to put her through rigorous special training, Shin-heung must navigate a series of ridiculous situations and a cast of hilarious characters.
title_norm:日本的悲劇:
Color | 101 min | 2012
IFF Rotterdam 2012, Busan IFF 2012
Special Mention, 2013 Osaka Asian Film Festival

After the sudden passing of his beloved wife and with his dejected only son facing middle-aged unemployment, an ailing old carpenter realizes his days are numbered. He decides to nail his bedroom door shut and starve himself, instructing his son not to break in until he finds a job so they can continue collecting pension payments to survive. What was once a blissful three-generation household is now fractured by death and mired in suffering; their lives have lost all color overnight. Separated by a single door, can the father and son rediscover their bond, regain the will to live, and see their journey through to the end?

At 80 years old, Tatsuya Nakadai remained a formidable force on screen and stage. Here, he delivers a raw, unadorned performance as a grieving father who has lost the will to live. Through a series of intense close-ups, he masterfully captures the character’s profound despair. He is joined by the talented Kazuki Kitamura and Berlin Silver Bear winner Shinobu Terajima, who both deliver standout performances. Following *Haru’s Journey*, which similarly explored themes of aging and mortality, Nakadai and director Masahiro Kobayashi reunite for this adaptation of a notorious true case, casting a spotlight on the harsh realities of Japan’s aging society. Kobayashi tailored the role specifically for Nakadai, approaching the film with the gravity of writing a final testament. The result is a heavy yet authentic exploration of life and death that confronts the psychological trauma of the post-311 era.
title_norm:早餐俱樂部: I hope the weather is beautiful. See you on the rooftop.
title_norm:書店裡的影像詩ⅲ:
★ 2024 Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival ★
*Poetries from the Bookstores Season 3*

Director Hou Chi-jan curates forty bookstores located across cities, villages, and offshore islands. In these distinct spaces, he replaces words with images to compose visual poetry. At times featuring conversation or song, and at others letting ambient sounds flow naturally, the series employs a clean, minimalist aesthetic to capture people, books, and spaces. With a gentle and melodic rhythm presented in varying lengths, it is like reading a visual poem of Taiwan’s bookstore landscape—rich, moving, and profoundly heartwarming.
title_norm:極限返航: An unexpected choice, an impossible mission.
title_norm:樂一通大戰外星人 粉紅末日 國語配音版: Roommates Daffy Duck and Porky Pig discover a massive hole in their roof and, thanks to a lead from Petunia Pig, land jobs at a bubblegum factory to earn the repair money. However, they accidentally discover that the new pink bubblegum hitting the shelves turns anyone who eats it into a zombie! Their investigation reveals a sinister plot by the evil alien "Mojo Jojo," leaving this ragtag team as the world's only hope. The most dangerous space rescue mission in history is about to begin!
title_norm:樂齡族電影院 大名倒產: By a stroke of luck, Matsudaira Koshiro unexpectedly becomes the lord of the Echigo Nyuyama Domain, only to discover he has inherited a staggering debt of 10 billion yen. They say money makes the world go round, but without it, life is a relentless grind. Since ancient times, the struggle for wealth has been a universal human challenge, and Koshiro is no exception. This engaging story follows Koshiro as he navigates this financial crisis, working alongside his friends to flip their fortunes and turn their lives around.
title_norm:樂齡族電影院 神選之地: In the late 19th century, a Danish priest travels to a remote part of Iceland with the mission of building a church and photographing its people. As he treks across the rugged, unforgiving landscape, the overwhelming forces of nature begin to erode his faith and ideals. Even as he settles into a small community to begin his ministry, the deeper he immerses himself in local life, the more he is confronted by human nature and temptation. Like the inverted images in a camera obscura, these forces distort his sense of purpose, leaving him adrift. With the harsh winter fast approaching, where will this journey ultimately lead him?
title_norm:機動戰士鋼彈 閃光的哈薩威 喀耳刻的魔女:
U.C. 0105. Twelve years after Char’s Rebellion, the anti-Federation organization "Mafty" resists the Earth Federation Government’s oppressive rule through a campaign of assassinations targeting high-ranking officials. Its leader is none other than Hathaway Noa, the son of Bright Noa, who once fought alongside Amuro Ray during the One Year War. 

Hathaway finds his past traumas resurfacing after witnessing the mysterious power of a young woman named Gigi Andalucia. Influenced by her words and grappling with inner conflict, he prepares for Mafty’s next major operation: an assault on the high-level meeting in Adelaide.
title_norm:歌喉讚: ☀️ I hope the weather is beautiful; see you on the rooftop.
title_norm:殺戮戰場的邊緣:
Beginning in 1980, a massive influx of Cambodian and Vietnamese refugees fled the horrors of war to the Thai-Cambodian border, establishing makeshift camps. Five years later, a team from Taiwan’s Kuangchi Program Service traveled to the region, capturing the harrowing reality of refugees risking their lives in minefields to forage for supplies, as well as their resilience as they used song and dance to soothe the spirits of the departed amidst the roar of artillery. As the first Taiwanese documentary to focus on international refugees, it broke the long-standing monopoly of state-owned studios on the Golden Horse Award for Best Documentary and served as a catalyst for the redefinition and critical discussion of the genre in Taiwan.

1986 Golden Horse Awards: Best Documentary, Best Documentary Director
1986 Asia Pacific Film Festival: Best Short Film

title_norm:比爾道格拉斯三部曲:
**My Childhood**
Bill DOUGLAS｜UK｜1973｜DCP｜B&W｜56min
1972 Venice Film Festival – Best First Film
1973 Writers' Guild of Great Britain – Best Original Screenplay

In a bleak, declining mining town, eight-year-old Jamie and his half-brother are raised by their maternal grandmother. Their mother has been long confined to a sanatorium, while their distant father lives nearby with another family. Young Jamie endures extreme poverty and isolation until he befriends a German prisoner of war, a connection that brings a glimmer of warmth to his dark childhood. Drawing from his own memories for this award-winning debut, the director captures a protagonist whose mud-streaked, sorrowful face evokes the lost youth of Antoine Doinel in Truffaut’s *The 400 Blows*—a work of heartbreaking sincerity.

**My Ain Folk**
Bill DOUGLAS｜UK｜1973｜DCP｜B&W｜72min
1973 BFI London Film Festival
1974 Berlin International Film Festival (Forum) – OCIC Award & Interfilm Award (Special Recommendation)

Following the death of his maternal grandmother, young Jamie is forced apart from his brother. While his brother is sent to an orphanage, Jamie is moved into his paternal grandmother’s home. His new family environment is cold and hostile; caught between his father’s absence, his grandmother’s cruelty, and the family’s chaotic dynamics, Jamie sinks deeper into loneliness. Life feels like a silent black-and-white film, and he finds refuge in the cinema, seeking salvation in the Technicolor dreams on the screen. Premiering alongside the first installment at the Berlin Film Festival to critical acclaim, this film solidified the arrival of a major new Scottish auteur.

**My Way Home**
Bill DOUGLAS｜UK｜1978｜DCP｜B&W｜72min
1978 BFI London Film Festival
1979 Berlin International Film Festival (Forum) – FIPRESCI Prize
1979 Locarno Film Festival

Now an adolescent, Jamie is sent to an orphanage by his paternal grandmother’s family, spending years drifting between social welfare institutions and foster homes. As an adult, he enlists in the military and is stationed in Egypt, where he meets Robert, a fellow soldier from a wealthy background. Bathed in the North African sun, the two bond over literature and film, developing an intimate friendship that transcends class boundaries. In the final chapter of the trilogy, the protagonist escapes the oppression of Scotland, finding mutual support and a sense of belonging in a foreign land. After years of wandering, the lost boy finally finds his way home.

*The screenings of the trilogy include a 10-minute intermission.*
title_norm:流光剪影 雪美蓮的影像記憶:
**A Very Easy Death**
Mary STEPHEN｜Canada｜1975｜DCP｜B&W, Color｜9min

**Pawaganak: The Great Canadian Puberty Rite**
Mary STEPHEN｜Canada｜1974｜DCP｜B&W, Color｜19min

**Shades of Silk**
Mary STEPHEN｜France, Canada｜1978｜DCP｜Color｜62min

2025 Toronto IFF
2025 New York FF
2026 IFF Rotterdam

Long before her legendary tenure as Éric Rohmer’s long-time editor, Mary Stephen was already a "tailor of images," using her camera to capture the displacement of the diaspora, the struggle for identity, and the growing pains of coming of age. This screening features four of her early works, including her debut feature *Shades of Silk* and three rare shorts of distinct styles—*Labyrinth*, *A Very Easy Death*, and *Pawaganak: The Great Canadian Puberty Rite*. Through the interplay of sound and image, Stephen transforms personal experience into evocative visual poetry. From a Canadian road-trip baptism and the somniloquy of a Parisian student dorm to a quiet gaze at death, her imagery is as delicate and resilient as silk. These works serve as memory fragments drifting between Eastern and Western cultures, documenting her perception and search for selfhood.
title_norm:流離之岸 1877 cepo 戰役 索: In 1999, an old DV tape plays footage of Chief Lekal Makor recounting a massacre buried for a century. The event took place in 1877, during the late Qing Dynasty, at Cepo'—the mouth of the Xiuguluan River in eastern Taiwan. Guided by the oral histories of tribal elders, the historical truth is gradually brought to light as the descendants of Cepo' retrace their ancestors' footsteps, seeking to piece together and reinterpret this legacy of memory and trauma.
title_norm:海豚男孩與怪物:
★ Winner of Best Animated Feature and the Audience Award at the 2025 Fajr International Film Festival
★ Global Box Office: 14 Million TWD

Dolphin Boy and his companions continue their relentless battle against the monsters of the deep. Their journey takes an unexpected turn when a villager named Majeed discovers a message in a bottle containing clues about a mysterious potion, leading them toward a brand-new unknown. During their voyage, they encounter a massive whale, and Majeed goes missing in the chaos.

As Dolphin Boy embarks on a perilous rescue mission, he learns that his father may be nearby. Driven by the hope of finding his family and uncovering the secrets of his origins, he resolutely ventures into even deeper waters. After Jid drinks the potion and transforms into a terrifying monster, Dolphin Boy—with the help of allies including the Navigator, his wife Leila, and the islanders—must face his greatest challenge yet to finally defeat Majeed.
title_norm:海邊的貓咪偵探社:
Starring Hikaru Makishima (*Extremely Inappropriate!*) and Masato Wada (*Rikuoh*). 

When Nekozuka’s cat goes missing, he seeks help from a pet detective agency. After an investigation, the detective, Sawatari, discovers that the cat is now living happily with a married couple. Unable to afford the investigation fee, Nekozuka has no choice but to work at the agency to pay off his debt. One day, a young boy named Yuta comes to the agency for help because his cat is missing. Yuta’s parents are currently undergoing divorce mediation; having grown up with divorced parents himself, Nekozuka deeply empathizes with the boy’s feelings. Nekozuka and Yuta set out together to find his cat, Gonta, and when they finally do, a miracle occurs at Yuta’s home...
title_norm:深度安靜:
★ Nominated for seven awards at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards, including Best New Director, Best Cinematography, Best Art Direction, and Best Leading Actor and Actress.

Yu-ming and Yi-ting first met in the "Deep Quiet Room" of their university library. They fell in love and married, expecting a stable life together. However, after Yi-ting becomes pregnant, past pressures and family shadows gradually resurface, fundamentally altering their relationship. When Yi-ting’s mobility-impaired father moves in, Yu-ming struggles to hold the family together, living through a suffocating existence of polite but distant formalities. Unable to truly understand Yi-ting’s inner world, it is only when Yu-ming reads the book she is currently editing that he realizes the burden she carries is far beyond anything he had ever imagined.
title_norm:為一切人，成為一切:
In 1952, during the arduous post-war years in Taiwan, over a hundred French and Swiss priests chose to serve in the Hualien and Taitung regions—the areas most lacking in resources at the time. They immersed themselves in indigenous communities, living alongside the residents while learning their languages and traditional cultures. In times of hardship, they provided a sanctuary for the local people, dedicating their lives to serving those in need. 

Long before the preservation of indigenous languages became a prominent social issue, these priests had already begun compiling dictionaries and conducting Mass in native tongues, effectively documenting tribal histories. Their work has since become an invaluable historical resource for Taiwan’s cultural and linguistic research. Seventy years later, amidst the shifting tides of Taiwanese society, some priests have been forced to depart, yet Fathers Liu Yi-feng and Dai Hong-ji remain on the front lines, continuing their mission to care for the most vulnerable.
title_norm:烈火青春 4k修復導演版:
Hong Kong International Film Festival 2023 | New York Asian Film Festival 2023 | Tokyo International Film Festival

Featuring a rising Leslie Cheung, a newly famous Ken Tong, and the screen debuts of Pat Ha and Cecilia Yip, this film follows four young people—two men and two women from both privileged and working-class backgrounds—who live boldly and love fiercely. Amidst a landscape of nihilism, disorder, and desire, they lead a modern nomadic life in the city. However, their world is upended when a defector from the Japanese Red Army, a radical far-left organization, unexpectedly appears, plunging them into a lethal crisis.

A provocative masterpiece by Hong Kong New Wave director Patrick Tam, the film caused a sensation upon its original release for its bold eroticism. With a script crafted by a team of legendary Chinese screenwriters, it employs Nietzschean thought to portray the restless youth and sexual liberation of the 1980s. Echoing the rebellious "Sun Tribe" (Taiyozoku) subculture of 1950s Japan, it has become an enduring and mesmerizing cult classic. To mark its 41st anniversary, the director has re-edited the film, presenting a definitive 4K restored version.

On Christmas Eve, innocent and carefree Lynne goes on an outing with her father and brother to a derelict railway on the edge of town. Lynne is initially excited and curious about her new playmates, until a boisterous pub gathering where she watches a strange little girl nestle in her father's arms. Lynne Ramsay’s second award-winning short at Cannes captures the complexities of the adult world through a child’s naive perspective. With masterful use of close-ups and sensory soundscapes, it tells a childhood tale of growth and disillusionment. Its poetic audio-visual direction and natural performances by non-professional child actors foreshadowed her stunning feature debut the following year, *Ratcatcher*.

In 1970s Glasgow, a massive garbage strike has left the streets infested with rats and a lingering stench. Twelve-year-old James is playing by the canal with a friend when a sudden accident occurs, causing him to flee in panic and bury his guilt in silence. He spends his days wandering, forming innocent bonds with a bullied, love-starved girl and a naive neighbor boy. Drifting between a dysfunctional home and decaying street corners, he yearns to escape his bleak reality. At night, he dreams of his pet rat ascending into the cosmos on a red balloon; by day, he boards a bus to nowhere, escaping his desolate housing estate to find a moment of peace in the distant fields.

Lynne Ramsay’s breathtaking debut feature showcases her unique poetics of audio-visual displacement. title_norm:物質世界 策展人開講:
**Curator’s Talk: "The Material World"**

"Curator’s Talk" is a series hosted by the Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM), inviting curators to provide in-depth guided tours and share their insights on specific exhibitions. In this session, curator Feng Hsin will lead an exploration of four thematic works within "The Material World."

**Event Time:** Saturday, July 11, 2026, 2:00 PM – 3:30 PM
**Venue:** 2nd Floor Exhibition Rooms, TFAM
**Check-in Location:** Entrance of Exhibition Room 2B
**Capacity:** 20 participants

**About the Event**
Matter shapes the way we live. From the moment we open our eyes, we are surrounded by material objects: the cups we drink from, the clothes we wear, the spaces we inhabit, and the smartphones that have evolved far beyond mere communication tools. Every facet of daily life—food, clothing, housing, transportation, and entertainment—is defined by matter. To meet the demands of life, objects are constantly created, invented, improved, and evolved. Humans use objects, and through that use, systems emerge. These systems, in turn, become intuitive actions in our daily lives; our postures, habits, and even our modes of thought are influenced by the things we use.

From Jean Baudrillard’s revelation of "sign value" in consumer society in the 1970s to Tim Dant and Bernard Stiegler’s exploration of "material practice" in the 1990s, matter is more than just a commodity or a reference of meaning. Through daily operation, use, and perception, it forms "object-derived technologies" that influence human patterns of action and the very fabric of society.

This exhibition looks back at the transition from agricultural to industrial and commercial society, examining how the production and circulation of matter have profoundly altered our world—from individual lifestyles to the large-scale mechanisms and hidden forces that drive social operations. We explore how matter continues to "generate" the world across different scales and perceptions, and how artists of different eras have translated the sensibilities of their times into material creations and experimental presentations, responding to the shifting perceptions and imaginations that accompany these changes.

**About the Speaker**
**Feng Hsin** is an Assistant Curator at the Taipei Fine Arts Museum. Her recent research focuses on the development of sound art, new media art, and contemporary cultural performance in Taiwan, as well as how digital technology influences public behavior and perception. 

Selected curatorial projects include: *Historical Variations* (2018, TKG+ Project), *Dynamic Layers* (2021, Museum of Contemporary Art Taipei), *Offline Reality* (2022, FreeS Art Space), and *Everyday Performance* (2024, Chiayi City Museum). She served as co-curator for the 2023 Romantic Route 3 Art Festival ("Travelers on the Foothills") and *Visible/Audible: Exhibition of Artifacts from Taiwan’s Film and Audiovisual History* (2022, Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute). She is also the co-author and editor of *Twenty Years of Contemporary Art Curating in Taiwan* (2015).

title_norm:狂飆與反叛 畫室外的陳來興、姚瑞中、劉秋兒 ｜陳文彬、姚瑞:
Artists who grew up during the Martial Law era found themselves at the heart of a turbulent society when the ban on newspapers was lifted in 1987, Article 100 of the Criminal Code was amended, and street movements began to surge. They threw themselves into these movements, their actions becoming a vibrant presence in the midst of social unrest. During this period, art served as an invisible pillar of support for street activism and social change. Artist Chen Lai-hsing donated works on several occasions at fundraising dinners for Chen Wan-chen—who had secretly returned to Taiwan while on the "blacklist"—and later co-founded the Taiwan Teachers’ Union with Lin Shuang-bu. During the commemorative exhibition for the May 20 Movement, Chen, along with Lin Cho-shui, Wu Mali, and Hou I-cheng, transformed the old Beitou Station into a gallery, treating "the street" as the ultimate venue for their art.

In the 1990s, performance art expanded its impact through the infiltration of public spaces and the promotion of "alternative art spaces," using art as a foundation to collide with social structures. Yao Jui-chung, wandering through landscapes of decay, used his camera to capture various forms of ruins across Taiwan, witnessing the transformation of industrial ruins into cultural and creative parks. For Yao, the restless 1990s became the catalyst for his "Ruin Enlightenment," leading him to write that "everything will become the ruins of the future." Meanwhile, Liu Chiu-er hosted an underground radio station in the 1990s and later established the "Dogpig Art Cafe" in Southern Taiwan, embedding his community energy and artistic activism into the shifting artistic landscape of Kaohsiung.

This forum invites director Chen Wen-pin, who is currently filming a documentary on Chen Lai-hsing, alongside artists Yao Jui-chung and Liu Chiu-er. Together, they will reflect on their firsthand experiences in street art movements and youthful rebellion, while delving into Taiwan's evolution from "spatial de-martialization" to contemporary cultural policy. Through the perspectives of these three speakers, we will re-examine that pivotal era of history and reflect on the core meaning of "art as social infrastructure."

**Location:** Multi-function Hall
**Speakers:** Chen Wen-pin, Yao Jui-chung, Liu Chiu-er

title_norm:狸想世界: Scientists have developed a way to "upload" human consciousness into hyper-realistic robotic animals, allowing users to communicate and interact with wildlife from their perspective. Mabel, an animal-loving college student, takes this opportunity to inhabit a robotic beaver. Through this experience, she meets King George the beaver and begins to learn the laws of the animal kingdom, including the seemingly zen "Pond Code." During her journey, she uncovers a sinister conspiracy: Mayor Jerry plans to develop the natural habitat, threatening to destroy the animals' homes. Mabel decides to take a stand, but can she and her animal companions successfully save their sanctuary?
title_norm:獨奏者之舞: Li Zhe-yang was a youth of the 1950s White Terror era who endured a lifetime of suppression, yet he forged a singular and extraordinary path through the thorns. A pioneer of the Taiwan Folk Song Collection Movement, he spent nearly twenty years as the editor-in-chief of *Music Digest* and translated a vast body of musical literature. By spreading the wisdom and beauty of music, he profoundly influenced generations of Taiwanese music lovers from the 1970s through the 1990s. However, his solitary journey through the world of music has been largely forgotten by the history of Taiwanese music.
title_norm:王命之徒: The Gyeoyu Jeongnan coup shakes the foundations of Joseon, forcing the young King Yi Hong-wi (Park Ji-hoon) to abdicate and face exile. Meanwhile, in the remote mountain village of Gwangcheongok in Yeongwol, Gangwon Province, village head Eom Heung-do (Yoo Hae-jin) strives to have Cheongnyeongpo designated as an exile site to support his struggling villagers. Amidst the village head’s great expectations, the deposed Yi Hong-wi finally arrives. Tasked with monitoring the former king's daily life, Eom finds himself increasingly drawn to the young man, who has lost all will to live. In 1457 at Cheongnyeongpo, a doomed effort to protect him begins—a bond that will be remembered forever.

title_norm:生命接力賽: Based on a true story, 14-year-old best friends Ari and Sara are facing life-altering challenges. title_norm:畫外流離 革命直至勝利:
Driven by curiosity and a lack of familiarity with Palestinian cinema and history, a film student uses the 1948 "Nakba" (Day of Catastrophe) as a watershed moment, navigating the battles and struggles of the Palestinian people through archival footage. Beginning with classics such as Jean-Luc Godard’s *Notre Musique*, the film pieces together a destiny spanning over 40 years. Composed entirely of Palestinian footage screened at international film festivals prior to 1982, the work directly highlights the techniques and significance of repurposing "displaced images."

A meditation on Palestinian self-representation through the Palestine Film Unit (PFU) of the 1960s–70s. Drawing on globally recovered archival footage, the film traces militant filmmakers reclaiming image and narrative through revolutionary cinema, reflecting on struggles revived on screen—and those that remain off frame.

title_norm:神木之島:
Following *Black Bear Forest*, Golden Horse Award-winning director Li Hsiang-hsiu returns with another documentary capturing the stories of Taiwan's wilderness. The film follows canopy epiphyte researcher Rebecca Hsu and "The Tree Hunters," a team she leads that is dedicated to locating Taiwan’s tallest trees.

Tracking the team’s expeditions, the film traverses Taiwan’s remote wilderness from north to south, including the Chilan Mountains, the upper reaches of the Da’an River, the Taigang River in Bianjiyan, the Taoshan and Shilun Mountain areas, the Daxueshan Forest Road, the Kashe River basin along the Danda Forest Road, the Ka’alang River, and the region around Dagui Lake and Mount Benye.

Beyond documenting the search itself, the film captures the creation of a life-sized portrait of the "Taoshan Giant Tree" and the intricate process of dismantling logging cables. This documentary provides a rare look at how the team locates these giants in the deep wilderness, how they predict tree heights before setting out, and the death-defying climbs required to measure them manually.

A father and son travel to the edge of the desert in southern Morocco in search of a long-lost relative. Shanghai, 1949. As ships prepare to set sail for the other side of the Strait, Grandma follows her son-in-law, a General, to relocate to Taiwan amidst the chaos of war. Their new home boasts a sprawling courtyard where fireflies illuminate their smiles at night. Grandma meticulously cares for her many grandchildren, ensuring the family remains warm and well-provided for. After recovering from his wounds, the General retires from military life, while his wife busies herself making ends meet and prepares for the arrival of a new baby. As time passes and the grandchildren grow up, Grandma’s heart remains tethered to the memory of the fruit-laden red persimmon tree back in her Henan home.

Semi-autobiographical in nature, director Wang Tung returns to his own roots and history following his renowned trilogy. *Red Persimmons* depicts the daily lives of a military family retreating to Taiwan during the final stages of the Chinese Civil War.
title_norm:綠星人大鬧巴黎城:
The inhabitants of the Green Planet hold an annual summit to decide who will be sent on scouting missions to other planets, but Earth is the one place nobody wants to go. Having not visited since the 19th century, the Green Planet people are horrified by modern-day Earth. With streets swarming with bizarre objects called "cars" and a backward civilization that still uses money, no one is willing to face such grueling conditions.

As the meeting reaches a stalemate, Mila raises her hand to volunteer. It turns out she is half-human and wants to use this opportunity to learn more about the world where her late mother was born and raised. But after landing in Paris, she finds herself completely disoriented and blissfully indifferent to human rules. Thus begins a chaotic, whirlwind adventure through the City of Light.

Coline Serreau serves as both director and lead actress, portraying Mila. By contrasting a harmonious, simple utopia with an Earth dominated by materialism and technology, the director uses alien culture shock to satirize the alienation between humans, their environment, and one another, posing profound questions about the true meaning of human well-being.

Winner of Best Director, the Marcello Mastroianni Award, and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Venice Film Festival, as well as a Blue Dragon Award for Best New Actress and an Independent Spirit Award nomination for Best Foreign Film. Dejected and alone, he visits the home of the victim’s family, where he meets the daughter, Han Gong-ju, who suffers from severe cerebral palsy. Despite her physical contortions, Jong-du finds himself drawn to her, leading to an impulsive and bold encounter. Though society views them as "abnormal" or "broken," they possess a purity of heart that is constantly tested by a series of social injustices. Will fate finally stop toying with their lives? title_norm:綠的海平線 軍教男兒－台灣軍士教導團的故事:
At the end of World War II, more than 8,000 Taiwanese youths were mobilized by the Japanese government to produce military aircraft at naval factories. In the post-war era, they stood in the fissures between different times and regimes; though their chosen paths varied, they all faced the same grueling struggle to adapt and survive. Facing the weight of history, the film avoids resentment and pathos, opting instead for a warm narration to thread together archival documents and interviews. It gently unfolds the personal strivings and helpless drifts of individuals in a turbulent age, reflecting the complex, overlapping layers of identity and belonging.

**Suspended Duty: Taiwan Military Training Regiment**
KUO Liang-yin｜Taiwan｜2010｜DCP｜Colour｜47 min

During the era of "Resisting Communism and Opposing Russia," over 4,000 young men joined the "Taiwan Military Training Regiment" in 1950, expecting to serve as cadres for a new Taiwanese army upon completing their training. Before long, they were hit with a sudden order of "suspended duty," leaving them on standby for over 50 years without ever being formally discharged. Using a satirical, propaganda-style narration to humorously bridge various interviews, the film reveals how political forces discipline the body, silence dissent, and manipulate thought. Through the firsthand accounts of those who lived through different wars, it invites a deeper contemplation on the question: "For whom do we fight?"

title_norm:聽．視界電影院 幸福巧克力: This moving documentary chronicles the true story of how a bakery owner, driven by a mission to support marginalized communities, founded Quon Chocolate. Quon Chocolate stands in a league of its own, with founder Koji Natsume’s ingenuity reflected in the brand’s diverse and creative offerings. title_norm:聽．視界電影院 滿分之一秒: Can you let go of the pain of the past and move toward the future? Handpicked by the head coach, Jae-woo has made it to the finals of the national Kendo team selections. title_norm:聽．視界電影院 羅馬時光機: Rome, 1829. Bartolomeo is a wealthy and greedy man who covets a noble title above all else. In order to strike a secret deal with Prince Accoramboni and win the hand of his daughter in marriage, Bartolomeo must journey through the past, present, and future, overcoming a series of trials. Aided by several extraordinary companions, he will come face-to-face with his true self and discover a brand-new meaning to life.
title_norm:聽．視界電影院 速命道:
An ambulance and a mysterious sports car known as the "Hellcat" engage in a high-stakes duel, tearing from the docks and mountain passes onto the open highway. Within the city, their battle mirrors a legendary clash of masters atop Mount Wudang. Who will emerge as the next "God of Racing"? If only one can survive, who will have the last laugh?

Behind the wheel of the ambulance is Xiao Le, once a premier racer. After a tragic accident during a race with his older brother, Ah Jie, resulted in his brother's death, Xiao Le spiraled into self-destruction. It wasn't until he met Dr. Hui Hui that he found a new path, becoming an ambulance driver and vowing to "use speed to save lives."

However, the mysterious owner of the "Hellcat" has suddenly appeared, wielding a hit list of racers. Every driver he challenges meets a fatal end. Underground racing is a modern-day martial arts world; even when the price is life itself, it cannot stop these fanatics from their fateful pursuit of speed. As Xiao Le’s best friend, San Bao, begins to investigate, the hidden truth behind these accidents slowly comes to light.
title_norm:聽．視界電影院 鐵幕追緝令: Based on a true case from 1979, an investigator encounters one of the most terrifying serial killers in history. Set in the borderlands of Soviet Kazakhstan, rookie detective Sher Sadykov is assigned to a special tasks unit. His first case involves a serial killer who targets women. As the number of victims continues to rise, the investigation reaches a standstill—until Sher discovers that the killer has chosen his next target: his sister, who lives with him.

Constantly rushing between rehearsals, performances, and work, the lead singer of the indie band "Abandoned Field" refuses to let himself slow down. Within his restless body lurks a shadow passed down through his family’s blood. On stage, he pours his entire soul into every scream; off stage, he simply longs to be a free man.

Philippe is an uninspired opera composer forced to take in his niece, Simone, a rebellious and eccentric orphan whose best friend is a skunk. Despite their polar opposite personalities, Philippe and Simone soon discover that they might need each other more than they ever imagined.
title_norm:舞林殺手:
Award-winning director Eiji Uchida strikes again with a genre-defying masterpiece that blends high-octane assassin action with the art of dance. A motley crew of professional assassins, each with vastly different ages and temperaments, accepts a high-stakes, big-money contract. Their target is the notorious mob boss Heizo Honjo, but there’s a catch: the only way to get close to him is by winning a dance competition!

With zero experience, no chemistry, and even less motivation, can this ragtag team actually compete in a serious dance tournament? Assembled solely because they supposedly had "prior dance experience," this eccentric squad features: Daiya, an orphanage counselor who is secretly a legendary ex-assassin; Kumashiro, the mission recruiter and second-in-command of the Kazama Syndicate; Kiryu, a cold-blooded lone wolf who hates working in groups; Arata, a hot-headed but fiercely loyal hitman; and Murasame, a washed-up former yakuza. 

Though they initially clash at every turn, these killers soon find themselves seduced by the rhythm, transforming into a formidable force of "dance-floor assassins." As they fight their way through the rounds, will they actually dance their way to the championship?

A sparkling stone sparks a treasure-hunting craze among Edmond, Lucy, and their friends down by the river. As they search and compare their finds, they find themselves wanting more and more to take this "beauty" home. The witch Gothel kept Rapunzel hidden in a high tower deep within the Forbidden Forest, guarded by a dragon named Hugo and surrounded by an enchanted wall. Day and night, Rapunzel was at the beck and call of Gothel’s servants; her favorite passion, painting, could only be done in secret when no one was watching. By a twist of fate, Rapunzel accidentally discovers an ancient tunnel and, risking Gothel’s wrath, ventures out into the world alone. Twelve-year-old Felix is convinced that his father, who disappeared at sea two years ago, is still alive. Determined to find him, Felix sets out on a quest accompanied by Old Tom, a retired fisherman; Squawk, a thieving one-legged parrot; and Rover, a cat who acts just like a dog. However, seeing Apeksha fall in with the wrong crowd at school, Chanda constantly worries that her daughter might go astray. A young woman meets a British gentleman in a foreign land, falls head over heels, and marries him in a whirlwind romance. However, upon returning to his grand estate in Cornwall, she discovers the ancient manor is no honeymoon nest, but a labyrinth haunted by the shadow of his late wife. From the furnishings and old clothes to every corner of the house, everything seems to whisper her presence. As the young bride sinks into anxiety, the ice-cold housekeeper constantly reminds her that she can never replace her predecessor. When a shipwreck is salvaged and brought ashore, the lies and mysteries of death hidden deep within the estate begin to surface.

Alfred Hitchcock’s first American film, adapted from Daphne du Maurier’s 1938 novel of the same name, uses high-contrast black-and-white cinematography to recreate a world of suspense and obsession. Despite the strict constraints of the Hays Code, the film subtly touches on taboos such as marital infidelity and lesbian undertones. Du Maurier, a master of Gothic romance, possessed a style so influential that it inspired the novel *Mistress of Milan* (the basis for *Corpse Bride*) and even led some to believe she was its true author.
title_norm:蠱降: Malaysian real estate mogul Song Longchen uses Thai black magic to seize land development rights, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. Suspecting foul play, Thai journalist Fon launches an investigation. Meanwhile, four young content creators travel to Thailand to document local folklore, only to be plagued by terrifying supernatural occurrences and mysterious deaths upon their return. Fon deduces they have fallen victim to a curse and seeks the aid of the venerable Master Bai. As Song continues to expand his empire through a dark sorcerer, a climactic battle between black and white magic erupts.
title_norm:街頭巷尾 數位修復版:
1963 Golden Horse Award for Best Child Star. After the impoverished Lin A-sao passes away from illness, she leaves behind her young daughter, Xiao Zhu, with no one to turn to. Shi Santai, a scavenger, takes the girl under his wing. Together with pedicab driver Chen A-fa and the other residents of their crowded tenement courtyard, they support one another amidst the dilapidated alleys. As poverty, illness, and emotional entanglements strike in succession, can these ordinary people protect their way of life and each other?

This film was Lee Hsing’s first Mandarin-language feature and a pivotal turning point in his early career. He spent considerable time scouting locations and observing people, even leading the crew to scavenge old furniture for the sets in an effort to create a believable world within the tenement. Although primarily in Mandarin, the film retains fragments of Taiwanese Hokkien and features Hokkien cinema star Ho Yu-hua, leaving clear traces of Lee’s roots in Hokkien filmmaking. Cinematographer Lai Cheng-ying crafted meticulous visuals, marking the beginning of a long-term partnership between the two. By focusing on the slums and the working class, the film offers an early glimpse into the themes of social conditions, family ethics, and community bonds that would define Lee Hsing’s later work.

A man lives confined in a cramped room where the silence is suffocating. His thoughts drift through fragmented memories: the theft that led to his imprisonment, the desolate routine of prison life, the agony of withdrawal in a cell, senseless teenage acts of delinquency by a riverbank... and a single, golden childhood memory of playing in the fields with friends. Lynne Ramsay’s second short film marks the beginning of her deep fascination with marginalized and flawed characters. Through a disorienting non-linear narrative, overlapping soundscapes across different timelines, and tactile, sensory imagery, she portrays the withered body and chaotic inner world of an addict, furthering her aesthetic exploration of traumatic experiences and sensory fissures.

Morvern, a supermarket clerk, wakes up to find her boyfriend has committed suicide in their apartment, leaving behind a sum of money, a mixtape, and an unpublished manuscript. Instead of calling the police, she calmly cleans the scene, replaces his name with hers on the manuscript, and sends it to a publisher. Thus begins her journey. She and her best friend flee the cold, gloomy skies of Scotland for the sun-drenched coast of Spain. Wandering through disjointed and unfamiliar landscapes, she begins to grasp the root of her emptiness and the restless urge for self-exile. 

Adapted from the Somerset Maugham Award-winning novel, the film serves as a contemporary variation of Camus’s *The Stranger*. With a minimalist narrative and captivating cinematography, it dives deep into the protagonist’s strange state, oscillating between mourning and revelry. The film’s soundscape is driven by the boyfriend’s mixtape, featuring tracks by The Velvet Underground and Aphex Twin, using fragmented light and rhythm to articulate alienation and the drifting soul of a woman with nowhere to belong.
title_norm:讓建築歌唱～徐亞英的交響人生:
Renowned Chinese-American architectural acoustics master Xu Yaying spent decades collaborating with Pritzker Prize-winning legends such as I.M. Pei and Frank Gehry. Celebrated for his "invisible" acoustic designs, Xu contributed to the design and construction of nearly a hundred cultural and artistic venues worldwide. His late-career magnum opus—and the project he takes the most pride in—is Taiwan’s National Kaohsiung Center for the Arts (Weiwuying).

Architectural acoustics is a synthesis of physics, music, architecture, and science. An acoustician enables music to flow through a meticulously designed space, ensuring that beautiful melodies can truly move the human heart. Following Xu’s lean yet steady footsteps, we revisit his most iconic masterpieces, including the Louvre Pyramid and the Philharmonie Luxembourg. He recounts his journey of solving complex challenges for architects, revealing how he earned the nickname "Mr. Why Not" from Christian de Portzamparc.

title_norm:豬八戒與孫悟空:
Tang Sanzang and his disciples journey westward to retrieve sacred scriptures. Along the way, demons lay one trap after another, and Pigsy finds himself repeatedly swayed by worldly temptations. From the Mo Family Manor to the Silk Cave, the bond between the master and his disciples is frequently strained. How will the ever-troublesome Pigsy join forces with Sun Wukong to turn danger into safety?

Continuing the slapstick comedic style of the wildly popular *Brother Wang and Brother Lin on a Tour of Taiwan*, this film stands as one of director Li Hsing’s most significant works from his Taiwanese-language cinema period. The fact that Pigsy’s name precedes Sun Wukong’s in the title reveals the director's fondness for comic figures like Pigsy, as well as his early creative focus on "licorice" (supporting) characters and folk tales. Playing the role of Pigsy is none other than "Brother Wang" himself, Li Kuan-chang, who brings his signature comedic flair to the supernatural world of *Journey to the West*. The film’s songs are performed off-screen by the "Queen of Formosan Songs," Chi Lu-hsia, and others. Accompanied by on-screen lyrics, these musical numbers highlight the symbiotic relationship between Taiwanese-language films and the pop music market, as well as the central role music played in the moviegoing experience of the era. The production was completed at Ho Chi-ming’s Huaxing Studio.
title_norm:超人再起:
A "Superman" is someone who transcends themselves. While the first documentary, *Taiwan Superman*, chronicled those who overcame congenital limitations, *Superman Rising* turns its lens toward heroes facing severe acquired trauma. 

The film features a blind national athlete who shattered long jump records; a firefighter who suffered severe burns in the Kaohsiung gas explosions yet returned to his post; and a one-legged "Ironman" who, after losing a limb in a car accident, now challenges himself in land, sea, and air sports. It is difficult to imagine the immense courage required to navigate such hardships, yet these individuals did more than just endure—following their "rebirth," they reached out to support others walking similar paths. 

Through their stories, we see how scars are transformed into strength and witness the unwavering devotion of their families. We follow the life trajectories of these "Supermen" as they break through the darkness to face the light once more. This film is shared with the hope of continuing the empowering spirit that the *Taiwan Superman* series brings to us all.
